description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project is a rapid response mechanism and will provide lifesaving health and nutrition interventions in response to the Sudan crisis post-April 15, 2023, to the hotspot locations with emerging needs in Sudan. With food insecurity and famine in many localities, in addition to weak health systems. The project will allow quick response in hotspot areas with aim of reducing morbidity and mortality including among under five, maternal mortality and those associated with malnutrition by increasing access and coverage for people in needs with more focus on vulnerable groups such as children under five, pregnant and breastfeeding women. description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe Sudan IASC System Wide Scale Up (January-June 2026) and UN Medical Director’s Report (March 2026) jointly outline the critical, unmet need for strengthened emergency medical and medevac services in Darfur. The project will alsonbspdeliver capacity building for first responders, clinical staff and ambulance drivers on emergency triage, stabilization and first aid. title.narrative: Life-saving multi-purpose cash assistance in 9 hyper-prioritized IPC 4/5 localities in North Darfur, White Nile, North Kordofan and South Kordofan

description.narrative: ltpgtSudan continues to face a severe and rapidly deteriorating humanitarian crisis, with large populations in IPC Phase 4 and 5 across multiple states. Escalating conflict, displacement, market disruption and inflation have significantly reduced household purchasing power, leaving crisis-affected populations unable to meet basic food and non-food needs. In hyper-prioritized localities of North Kordofan, South Kordofan, White Nile and North Darfur, households face critical consumption gaps and heightened protection risks. Plan International, through United States Government funding managed by the UN OCHA-coordinated Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF), will implement six months of rapid and protection-sensitive cash delivery to populations facing the most acute humanitarian needs.ltbrgtThrough this intervention, Plan International Sudan will provide life-saving multi-purpose cash assistance to 70,000 crisis-affected individuals in 9 IPC 4/5 localities identified in the allocation framework. The intervention directly supports urgent consumption needs while mitigating negative coping strategies and protection risks.ltbrgtAssistance will be delivered through the following complementary modalities:ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtHousehold-level Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), delivered either through three monthly instalments or a one-off transfer. lt/ligtltpgtThe three-round cash is designed for protracted assistance to internally displaced persons (IDPs), vulnerable host communities and returnees in targeted locations. It provides the stability necessary for households to move beyond immediate survival, allowing them to plan their expenditures on food, non-food items, and healthcare over three months. The one-off transfer is aimed at newly displaced populations in the hotspots. It serves as a high-value, immediate financial injection to cover the "shock" costs associated with displacement.lt/pgtltligtGroup Cash Transfers (GCTs) to pre-existing community groups to enable rapid, community-led emergency responses addressing urgent food, nutrition, WASH and protection gaps. These groups include Mutual Aid Groups (MAGs), such as Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs), women’s groups and youth groups already active in local humanitarian response. Support will follow SHF procedures for engagement with community-based groups as outlined in the SHF Risk Absorption Note.lt/ligtltligtTargeted one-off protection cash assistance for individuals facing acute protection risks.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtTransfer values will be aligned with Sudan Cash Working Group (CWG) guidance and prevailing Minimum Expenditure Basket benchmarks (70% of the MEB for the 3 rounds transfer and 100% for one-off cash), taking into account market functionality and inflation trends. Modalities will be adapted based on security conditions, access constraints and operational feasibility to ensure timely delivery within the six-month implementation period. The design of the cash assistance component is informed by the Joint Market Monitoring Initiative (JMMI) conducted by the Sudan Cash Working Group in September 2025, which provided updated analysis on market functionality and Minimum Expenditure Basket values across the targeted localities.ltbrgtTargeting will follow community-based and protection-sensitive approaches aligned with inter-cluster prioritization and IPC analysis. Particular attention will be given to women-headed households, persons with disabilities, older persons, adolescent girls and other vulnerable groups. Where protection concerns are identified, referrals will be facilitated through established cluster-coordinated pathways. ltbrgtAccountability to affected populations will be embedded throughout the project cycle. ltbrgtPlan Sudan maintains established operational presence and partnerships in the targeted states, including experienced field teams and established financial service provider arrangements. This enables rapid scale-up and immediate implementation upon allocation approval.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Integrated Multi-Sectoral Emergency Response for IDPs and Host Communities in Tawila, Al Twisha, and Al Lait, North Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Integrated Multi-Sectoral Emergency Response Project is a six-month emergency intervention with a total budget of $2,500,000. It will be managed by Deutsche Welthungerhilfe (WHH) in collaboration with local partner SAHARI, the project provides rapid, lifesaving assistance to approximately 30,000 vulnerable individuals (IDPs and Host Communities) in Tawila, Al Twisha, and Al Lait, North Darfur. By leveraging an integrated multi-sectoral approach, the intervention addresses immediate survival needs through four key clusters: Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), Nutrition, Emergency Shelter/NFI, and WASH.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe core of the intervention is focused on Al Lait and Al Twisha, targeting 18,000 individuals (9,000 per locality). The Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (63% of the budget) provides 3,000 households with three consecutive monthly transfers of USD 145. This assistance empowers families to meet self-prioritized needs such as food and medicine while supporting local market functionality and reducing reliance on harmful "crisis" and "emergency" level coping strategies.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtComplementing the cash component, the Nutrition sector (15%) supports 7,000 beneficiaries in Al Lait and Al Twisha. Working with SAHARI, WHH will support eight nutrition centers to conduct community-based MUAC screenings, treat acute malnutrition (SAM/MAM), and provide Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) counseling to caregivers. This ensures a holistic approach where households have both the financial means to purchase food and the medical support to treat malnutrition.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn Tawila, the project addresses the acute needs of displaced populations facing severe gaps in living conditions. The Emergency Shelter and NFI sector (13%) will provide 3,000 individuals (500 households) with standard NFI kits and local construction materials to improve physical safety and dignity. Simultaneously, the WASH sector (9%) targets 2,000 IDPs in Tawila with emergency water trucking, ensuring a consistent supply of at least 15 liters of safe water per person per day to mitigate the risk of waterborne diseases in high-density displacement settings.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThroughout implementation, WHH will utilize its long-standing operational presence in North Darfur to ensure "Do No Harm" principles and protection mainstreaming. The project incorporates a robust Monitoring and Evaluation framework, featuring Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) and a community-based Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanism (FCRM). By utilizing the RedRose platform for cash transfers and partnering with national NGOs, the project ensures transparency, accountability, and the safe delivery of aid to the most marginalized groups, including female-headed households and persons with disabilities, even within a volatile security environment.ltbrgtlt/pgt

Newly displaced families arrive with no assets returnees face disrupted services. In Khartoum/Al Jazira, intermittent markets and income loss, inflation, and debt limit purchasing power, pushing negative coping strategies. In South Kordofan/North Darfur, insecurity and destroyed infrastructure strain health/WASH systems, raising malnutrition and disease risks.ltbrgtR1 Update: Fighting has escalated in Kauda between the armed Atoro group and SPLM-N forces, displacing mainly women and children into four areas: Western Kadugli, Heiban, Umdurein, and Delami. title.narrative: MPCA assistance in hyper-prioritised localities inter-sectoral severity localities in North Darfur, Northern State, and AJ Jazirah in Sudan.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project aims to deliver rapid, life-saving, and protection-centered MPC to highly vulnerable households in hyper-prioritized inter-sectoral severity localities in North Darfur (Tawila, Melit), Northern State (Ad Dabbah), and AJ Jazirah (Medani Al Kubra, Sharg Al Jazirah). Since April 2023, ongoing conflict, repeated displacement, economic collapse, and severe market disruption have significantly reduced household purchasing power and access to food, water, healthcare, shelter, and essential non-food items. Inflation, supply chain instability, and widespread livelihood loss have pushed families toward harmful coping strategies, including reduced food consumption, asset depletion, debt accumulation, child labor, early marriage, and heightened exposure to protection risks. ltbrgtThis intervention is designed to provide immediate relief through a regular MPC modalities tailored to context-specific vulnerabilities in North Darfur (Tawila, Melit), Northern State (Ad Dabbah) AJ Jazirah (Medani Al Kubra, Sharg Al Jazirah), IDPs and vulnerable host communities will receive regular MPC over two or one monthly installments to support stabilization and prevent further deterioration of living conditions. Eligible HHs in Al Jazira and North Darfur will receive regular MPCA over two cash disbursements. The first disbursement will cover two months of assistance, while the second will cover the remaining one month, providing beneficiaries with a total of three months of assistance. In NS, eligible households will receive a one-off MPCA payment covering the full three months of assistance inltspangt single disbursement, due to delays in obtaining the TA initiating the registration process.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtRI will implement vulnerability-based identification and registration processes across all targeted localities. RI will prioritize IDPs and highly vulnerable host community members. Coordination will take place with relevant local authorities, CCCM structures where applicable, and the CWG to ensure harmonization of transfer values, complementarity with other actors, and avoidance of duplication. The targeting coordination will also involve the FSL, Health, and Protection clusters to facilitate referrals, including for health cases and GBV survivors. ltbrgtAs outlined by Sudan Multisectoral Needs Assessment 2025, female headed HHs face higher vulnerability across Sudan as they are more exposed to conflict, have fewer financial resources and report lower access to basic services. For the MPCA intervention priority will be given to female-headed households, households caring for separated or unaccompanied children, elderly-HHs, persons with disabilities, PLW, and HHs facing acute protection risks. Targeting will ensure gender balance and inclusivity, with 6,500 female-HHs and 6,500 male-HHs included in the caseload, while maintaining prioritization based on vulnerability criteria. RI will ensure that at least 5% of the targeted caseload includes persons with disabilities, and that gender and age inclusion principles guide outreach, registration, and distribution. ltbrgtTransfer values will follow area-based MEB guidance as defined by the CWG. Households in North Darfur will receive regular MPC totaling 1,200,000 SDG (USD 358.52) distributed over 2 installments. In AJ Jazirah and Northern states, households will receive regular MPC totaling 1,215,000 SDG (USD 363) distributed over 2 installments for Al Jazirah and 1 installment for Northern State. These differentiated transfer values reflect contextual market conditions and vulnerability profiles. ltbrgtBefore implementation, RI will conduct rapid cash feasibility and market assessments FGDs in each targeted state to confirm market functionality, supply availability, price stability, and FSP capacity and liquidity. Security, access protection risk analyses will inform site selection and mitigation measures. If markets are found to be severely constrained modality adjustments will be made in coordination with relevant clusters ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Scaleup expansion of Multi sectoral life saving assistance in hyper-prioritized locations of Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtCARE Sudan proposes the scale‑up and expansion of multi‑sectoral, life‑saving assistance in hyper‑prioritized locations across Sudan, addressing the rapidly worsening humanitarian crisis driven by protracted armed conflict, mass displacement, market disruption, and the continued erosion of household coping capacities. In alignment with the 2026 CBPF Reserve Allocation, the project positions Multi‑Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) as the central response modality, enabling crisis‑affected households to meet essential needs with dignity, autonomy, and flexibility. As conflict conditions intensify, vulnerable populations—particularly women, girls, older persons, persons with disabilities, and conflict‑affected households—are experiencing increasingly limited access to food, basic household items, and essential health and protection services. This intervention aims to supportnbspnbsp73,908 individualsnbsp(12,318nbspHHs) (27,342 women, 13,312nbspGirls, 20,692 Men, 12,562 Boys) in 4 states South Darfur, East Darfur, Kassala, and Gadaref under 83 prioritized localitiesnbspthrough MPCA, reinforced by robust accountability, protection mainstreaming, and community engagement systems that ensure assistance is safe, inclusive, and tailored to diverse needs.ltbrgtTo strengthen community resilience and maximize the impact of cash transfers, the project integrates complementary activities that promote informed access to services, empower local structures, and uphold transparency. CARE will implement structured community engagement, ensuring that households understand the purpose, value, and process of MPCA, while also participating meaningfully in decision‑making and monitoring. Functional feedback and complaints mechanisms—adapted for safety, accessibility, and confidentiality will allow affected people to raise concerns, request information, or express preferences in their preferred format. Protection mainstreaming is embedded across all components, with GBV‑sensitive approaches, child safeguarding, andnbspdisability‑inclusive measures guiding targeting, distribution, communication, and monitoring.ltbrgtKey activities include the provision of MPCA, refresher training for CARE staff and community representatives on protection, accountability, safe programming, disability inclusion, and market‑based response standards, as well as ongoing post‑distribution monitoring to assess market trends, expenditure patterns, and household well‑being. Importantly, the project will establish and strengthen referral pathways for protection (including GBV and child protection), nutrition, and health services, ensuring that individuals identified with heightened risks or urgent needs can access appropriate, credible service providers. This referral component will be implemented in close coordination with existing humanitarian coordination structures and local partners to maintain safety, confidentiality, andnbspsurvivor‑centered principles.ltbrgtImplementation will occur over a six‑month period, fromnbsp March to August 2026, in areas where humanitarian needs are most acute and access remains feasible. Although the uploaded budget includes placeholder values pending final confirmation, the project dedicates 100% of its resources to the Multi‑Purpose Cash sector, directly supporting Humanitarian Response Plan Strategic Objective 1: providing timely, life‑saving assistance to crisis‑affected people. Through this scaled-upnbspMPCA intervention, CARE Sudan leverages its longstanding presence, community trust, and operational capacity to deliver principled, rapid, and people‑centered assistance. The project seeks to help households reduce harmful coping strategies, preserve dignity, and mitigate protection risks while addressing their most urgent and essential needs amid Sudan’s evolving and highly volatile crisis.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Safe and Dignified Cash-Based Assistance to Crisis-Affected Populations in Sudan's Darfur and Kordofan

description.narrative: ltpgtThe primary objective of this project is to deliver principled, multipurpose cash assistance to vulnerable populations in three Sudanese states—West and South Kordofan and Central Darfur—while maintaining strong community engagement, transparency, and protection mainstreaming approach. This initiative addresses urgent, life-saving needs in specific localities, as determined by the hyper-prioritization exercise led by clusters in Sudan. Aid will be provided according to humanitarian principles, adhering to the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) and the recommendations of national clusters and working groups. The project is designed to ensure access to essential goods and services through a cash and market-based approach, aiming to meet the most pressing needs of the beneficiaries, while at the same time stimulate and use the local markets and possibly leveraging a multiplier effect across in need communities. Moreover, the assistance aims to prevent conditions from worsening for the targeted households and to lower the chances that those will resort to harmful coping strategies that could create long-term impact on their livelihoods and greater protection risks. ltbrgtConcern team will facilitate robust community engagement in seven designated localities. Collaboration with local authorities and community representatives will focus on clear communication of objectives, securing permissions, and raising awareness about entitlements. Inclusive participation methods—including community meetings, focus groups, and interviews with key informants—will be employed to gather feedback from all segments of the population, especially on matters of security and protection. These insights will inform risk assessments and tailored mitigation strategies. Information about project goals, entitlements, and beneficiary selection will be shared transparently through meetings and distributed materials. Early introduction of feedback and complaint mechanisms, supported by flyers and banners, will ensure communities are well-informed and actively involved throughout the project cycle. ltbrgtThrough this engagement, 4,711 vulnerable households (around 28,266 individuals) will be supported with one lumpsum round of assistance as approved through CWG and HFU under exceptional circumstances considering operational context. Transfer values are determined in line with CWG recommendations, regional transfer values will be used as recommended in local currency but budgeted using the Bank of Khartoum exchange rate. Pre-identified Financial Service Providers (FSPs) will facilitate efficient cash distribution, with premises established to guarantee safe and equitable access for all, particularly vulnerable groups. Rapid market assessments will be conducted as a part of household registration in key areas, using key questions from the Stoplight market assessment, to ensure safe access, market functionality, and commodity availability. Ongoing coordination with the CWG and JIMMI initiative will monitor and address any market distortions. ltbrgtTargeting is conducted through a phased, transparent process: initial beneficiary lists are obtained from local authorities, then refined through community engagement and validation with leaders and groups. Vulnerability criteria are clearly explained and agreed upon, followed by registration and verification (where needed) by the MEAL team. The final beneficiary list is internally approved and validated with communities to correct any inclusion or exclusion errors prior to cash distribution. Protection mainstreaming is integrated at every stage, including risk analysis, regular updates to the risk register, and mitigation measures. Assistance delivery follows Concern’s Cash SoPs, ensuring proper coordination and timely support. Recipients are informed about internal feedback and complaint mechanisms during community sessions, maximising accessibility and transparency.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: SHF Scale up - DRC: Integrated Mine Action Response in Hyper-Prioritized Conflict-Affected Areas 2026

description.narrative: ltpgtExplosive ordnance contamination remains a major barrier to humanitarian access, safe movement, and the restoration of basic services across conflict-affected areas of Sudan. Since the outbreak of war, large parts of Khartoum and other affected states have experienced widespread explosive contamination, while several priority states have received little or no mine action response. As returns and humanitarian operations expand into newly accessible areas, the presence of unexploded ordnance poses a critical threat to civilians and humanitarian responders alike.nbsp ltbrgtThis six-month project will enable safe humanitarian access, life-saving service delivery, and safe returns by rapidly scaling emergency mine action capacity in hyper-prioritized conflict-affected localities. The intervention supports the objectives of the SHF Reserve Allocation to expand life-saving assistance and restore safe access to services in priority locations.nbsp ltbrgtAs life-saving direct assistance, the project will deploy two Multi-Task Teams (MTTs) to conduct emergency survey and clearance of explosive ordnance. One team will operate in Khartoum State and one in White Nile, prioritizing the clearance of critical civilian infrastructure such as roads, markets, schools, health facilities, IDP settlements, and return areas. Clearance activities—including non-technical survey, battle area clearance, building search and clearance, manual mine clearance, and explosive ordnance disposal—will restore freedom of movement and enable humanitarian partners to deliver multi-sector assistance.nbsp ltbrgtTo reduce the risk of explosive ordnance accidents among affected populations, the project will also expand explosive ordnance risk education (EORE). Four EORE teams will be deployed—two in Khartoum, one in North Kordofan, and one in Blue Nile—where little or no structured mine action response has occurred since the conflict began. Teams will deliver community and school-based sessions tailored for women, men, girls, and boys, promote safe behavior, and encourage community reporting of explosive hazards. Risk awareness will also be reinforced through radio messaging in priority localities to reach populations in areas with limited physical access.nbsp ltbrgtTo enable the operation and expansion of these life-saving activities, the project will undertake several activities to support the enabling environment for mine action. The project will explore ways to further support identification and referral of individuals affected by explosive hazards to appropriate services by strengthening linkages between mine action teams and existing health, rehabilitation, and protection service providers.nbsp ltbrgtTo ensure that emergency clearance can scale rapidly in response to evolving humanitarian needs, the project will also expand operational capacity within the mine action sector. This includes procurement of essential demining equipment to address current shortages limiting deployable teams, delivery of in-country 3 team leader training to increase the number of qualified operators able to lead clearance teams and trauma medics to support them, and limited refurbishment of the national Mine Action Training Center to enable safe and compliant delivery of technical training.nbsp ltbrgtThrough these integrated activities, the project will directly reach approximately 69,000 people with life-saving mine action services and contribute to safer access to infrastructure, humanitarian assistance, and return areas across hyper-prioritized localities in Khartoum, North Kordofan, Blue Nile and White Nile. nbsp ltbrgtBy reducing explosive threats and restoring safe access, the intervention will facilitate the delivery of humanitarian assistance and help create safer conditions for displaced populations and affected communities. ltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Multi-sectoral cash Assistance for conflict affected Populations in Khartoum and Blue Nile (MAP)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project will provide life-saving Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to conflict-affected and newly displaced populations in Khartoum and Blue Nile States, addressing acute food insecurity and immediate basic needs resulting from ongoing conflict, displacement, and economic collapse. The humanitarian situation across both states remains critical, with food security indicators reflecting severe deterioration of household resilience and purchasing power. Recent assessments show that in Blue Nile only 12% of households report an acceptable Food Consumption Score (FCS), while in Khartoum the average across targeted localities is 32%, masking sharp disparities between areas such as Jebel Awlia (49%), Khartoum locality (47%), and Omdurman (1%), where prolonged insecurity and disrupted markets have severely undermined food access. Similarly, the Reduced Coping Strategy Index (rCSI) highlights widespread reliance on negative coping mechanisms, with only 1% of households in Blue Nile and 4% in Khartoum reporting low reliance on harmful coping strategies. These findings demonstrate an alarming erosion of livelihoods and coping capacity, underscoring the urgent need for rapid and flexible cash assistance.ltbrgtThe project will support 48870 individuals through a combination of emergency one-off cash assistance and regular MPCA transfers, prioritizing newly displaced households, vulnerable returnees, female-headed households, and families facing severe livelihood disruption. The intervention will distribute USD 726,700 in multipurpose cash, enabling households to meet critical needs such as food, water, shelter, transport, health care, and communication costs while preserving dignity and choice. Emergency cash assistance will target households affected by sudden shocks and meet protection needs, while regular MPCA will support households with poor or borderline Food Consumption Scores, helping stabilize consumption and reduce reliance on negative coping strategies.ltbrgtBeneficiary selection will follow a shock-responsive targeting approach aligned with Cash Working Group guidance, allowing assistance to reach affected households within 72 hours to two weeks following a crisis event. ADRA and its local partner CORD will coordinate with community structures, humanitarian coordination platforms, and early warning systems, including IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix alerts and cluster reports, to identify newly displaced and highly vulnerable households. Eligibility will be verified through a rapid needs assessment focusing on key indicators such as recent displacement, loss of shelter or productive assets, high dependency ratios, and disrupted livelihoods.ltbrgtImplementation modalities will be adapted to local conditions. In Khartoum, where insecurity limits household verification, ADRA will apply geographic targeting in high-severity blocks across Omdurman, Khartoum locality, and Jebel Awlia, using verified referral lists from ERRs and community volunteers to accelerate emergency transfers of 545,000 SDG per household. In Blue Nile, rapid registration points will be established in Al Kurmuk, Baw, At Tadamon, and Ed Damazine to identify newly arrived and highly vulnerable households.ltbrgtCash transfers will be delivered through pre-qualified Financial Service Providers, including Bank of Khartoum (Bankak), Blue Nile Mashreg Bank, and Tawasul, supported by the RedRose digital platform for beneficiary management and transaction monitoring. By providing timely and flexible cash assistance, the project aims to stabilize food consumption, reduce reliance on negative coping strategies, and enable households to meet urgent basic needs while strengthening dignity, resilience, and local market recovery.ltbrgtlt/pgt

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project aims to reduce crisis related morbidity and mortality by ensuring timely and accountable access to food, health and nutrition assistance in prioritized high severity localities in Darfur. CRS will leverage its supply chain capacity and pre-positioned commodities and relationships with suppliers to procure, store, transport, and dispatch of food, health, and nutrition commodities to meet multi-sectoral needs of an estimated 755,182 vulnerable IDP and host community households. ltbrgtUnder the health sector, CRS will establish a common pipeline, procuring standardized kits and managing warehousing and inventory control across a warehouse network in Darfur. CRS will transport and dispatch Pharmaceutical Health Kits across approximately 100 health facilities, depending on the caseload identified in each health facility. Allocation will be informed by locality prioritization, the identified PIN for TSFP, and existing WFP coverage in the targeted areas across all Darfur states and West Kordofan, benefitting an estimated 407,957 individuals. ltbrgtUnder the nutrition sector, CRS will transport and dispatch 40,000 RUSF cartons, expected to reach approximately 64,000 children and PLW with moderate acute malnutrition, assuming an average 8-12 weeks treatment duration. Supplies will be delivered to frontline health actors who will provide health and nutrition services directly to affected populations.ltbrgtHealth and nutrition commodities will be sourced through international and regional procurement channels based on availability and lead times. CRS will retain limited capacity for local procurement. Supplies will move through a hub and spoke logistics system enabling delivery to partners and frontline responders through warehouse hubs in Ed Daein, Zalingei, and Tawila. The project allows adjustments to routing and dispatch schedules in response to access conditions. ltbrgtCRS will expand its emergency food assistance into underserved localities in North and Central Darfur, including Tawila, Dar as Salam, Um Baru and/or Melit, as access allows, and Wasat and Shamal Jabal Marrah, where CRS and other food actors are not operating. The project will deliver a combination of in-kind food and cash-for-food to 315,225 crisis affected people, including IDPs and host community members, with attention to households caring for unaccompanied and separated children. ltbrgtCRS will build on its partnership with World Relief (WR) to quickly scale into new locations. CRS will also launch a procurement process to identify and sign 1-2 service contracts with local organizations operational in target localities. CRS will manage procurement, warehousing, and transport to the Primary Distribution Point (PDP), while WR and selected service providers will conduct last mile activities. CRS will retain responsibility for risk and compliance, quality assurance, and project oversight. ltbrgtThe service contract model enables geographic expansion and reduces barriers for local and national actors to access funding for last mile delivery. While initial implementation will focus on North and Central Darfur, the model allows CRS to extend operations in South and East Darfur as conditions evolve. ltbrgtCRS will source food commodities through local and regional suppliers, including international procurement where required. Commodities will be managed through the PDP in Abeche, Chad, supported by contingency storage near the border and inside Sudan. Supplies will be transported to delivery points in West, Central, and North Darfur, where WR and contractors will access commodities for final distribution. ltbrgtAcross both components, CRS will apply inventory controls, documented handovers, and monitoring systems to mitigate diversion risks and ensure accountability. The project integrates protection mainstreaming and accountability to affected populations, including vulnerability based targeting, feedback and complaints mechanisms, post distribution monitoring, and referral pathways.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Multisectoral cash-based assistance response in Darfurs and Kordofans

description.narrative: ltpgtWith humanitarian needs escalating rapidly and IPC projections indicating catastrophic food insecurity conditions in early 2026, rapid multi-purpose cash assistance from Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC) and Group Cash Transfers (GCT), is required to enable displaced households across Darfurs and Kordofans to meet immediate life-saving needs. Mercy Corps proposes to provide rapid MPC and GCT to 97,788 individuals across the four states. ltbrgtltbrgtIn November 2025, conflict escalated in South and North Kordofan – shifting conflict lines to a new front. Active violence continues to impact communities across South and North Kordofan, as well as across locations in South and Central Darfur. Across Sudan, more than 33 million people are in need of humanitarian support, with over 9 million people internally displaced. The proposed project focuses on supporting vulnerable households in 9 localities out of the 100 localities classified as inter-sectoral severity 4 of 5, according to the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan – and out of 84 hyper-prioritized localities for urgent scale up as per the SHF Strategy Allocation. ltbrgtltbrgtIn Darfur and Kordofan, markets remain functional in many places, however prices are volatile, leaving households without purchasing power to meet minimum needs. Reports of severe acute malnutrition among children indicate dangerous food consumption gaps, while overcrowded hosting and displacement camp arrangements increase protection risks, particularly for women-headed households, the elderly, and people with disabilities. These challenges are life-threatening and urgent: insufficient food intake and lack of cash to access essential services, elevate malnutrition, illness and negative coping strategies. Immediate MPC and GCT is required to stabilize consumption, enable access to food, water, health services and shelter through functional local markets, and reduce protection risks while complementary referrals are in place to address urgent cases. ltbrgtltbrgtWithin the proposed proposal, Mercy Corps will support vulnerable individuals within hyper- prioritized localities in South and Central Darfur, as well and North and South Kordofan, with MPC to 11,398 households (68,388 individuals) and GCTs to 49 community groups (29,400 individuals). Initial planning per locality has been included, however depending on access constraints, shifting needs and localized liquidity challenges, support may be shifted between prioritized localities in the four states to ensure assistance in provided in a rapid, timely and safe manner. Localities have been identified in coordination with the Cash Consortium of Sudan (CCS) and Cash Working Group (CWG), and will continue to coordinate during implementation, as well as across responding partners. While MPC and GCT assistance will be unconditional, modality of transfer (cash, bank transfer, etc) will depend on the most appropriate, cost effective and safe modality per locality. lt/pgt

title.narrative: Integrated lifesaving multipurpose cash assistance to save lives and promote resilience in vulnerable populations in crisis- affected communities in South Darfur, East Darfur and Blue Nile

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project aims to respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of the vulnerable communities including IDPs, returnees and host communities in South Darfur (Rehaid Albirdi Nitega localities) East Darfur (Ad Du'ayn,nbsp Adila Yassin localities) and Blue Nile (Baw At Tadamon localities focusing on those facing food insecurity, impacted by the conflict and requiring basic services especially communities affected by complex and interlinked factors, severe malnutrition, and grave protection concerns, in a safe and dignified way.nbsp The gender-sensitive, protection-focused, and localization- responsive approach, to providing Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) will enhance the capacity of target groups to respond to both emerging and ongoing crises. The project will focus on strengthening food security, improve livelihoods and enhance household resilience for the vulnerable populations in localities. The project will improve food consumption and improve access to basic services through the provision on unconditional cash assistance. 8,087nbsphouseholds (48,523 individuals) will be reached with three rounds of MPCA including people with disabilities (6%, 2,911nbspindividuals), and at least 57% female beneficiaries.nbspltbrgtUnder standard NCWG guidance, MPCA is normally delivered through three separate monthly transfers. However, as part of the humanitarian response acceleration plan, World Vision Sudan previously received endorsement through NCWG consultations to combine the first two transfer cycles into a single payment (2+1 approach) to mitigate implementation start-up delays and the anticipated impact of the rainy season.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtConflict sensitivity will be systematically integrated throughout the project cycle. Local conflict dynamics will be regularly analyzed to ensure that targeting, distribution modalities and community engagement processes do not exacerbate tensions between IDPs, returnees and host communities. Transparent targeting criteria, community consultations and equitable caseload allocation will be applied to promote social cohesion and minimize risks of exclusion or perceived bias. Continuous engagement with community structures will help identify and address potential tensions early.ltbrgtProtection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse will be strictly upheld in line with World Vision safeguarding standards. Mandatory PSEA awareness sessions will be conducted for project staff, suppliers, community leaders, and volunteers to ensure understanding of safeguarding principles, expected conduct, and reporting channels. Accessible and confidential community feedback and complaints mechanisms will be established to enable safe reporting of concerns, including safeguarding incidents. Malak Gibreel (malak_gibreel@wvi.org) will serve as the designated PSEA focal point for the project, responsible for coordinating safeguarding awareness, monitoring compliance, and ensuring timely referral and response to any reported cases.nbspEffective feedback and accountability mechanisms will ensure timely resolution of grievances, conflicts, or concerns during project implementation, strengthening transparency and accountability to affected populations.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Scaling Up Multisectoral Cash and Protection Assistance in Hyper-Prioritised Locations of Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtWith the support of MOD, SZWO and HOPE, Acted will implement a locally led, protection-centered emergency, direct life-saving humanitarian response ltbrgtreaching 51,869 Individuals across 10 hyper-prioritised localities in seven states:ltbrgt Al Jazirah: Medani Al Kubra, Sharg Al Jazirahltbrgt Blue Nile: At Tadamon, Baw, Ed Damazineltbrgt Gedaref: Basundahltbrgt South Darfur: Buramltbrgt West Darfur: Habilalt/pgtltulgtltligtEast Darfur: Ad Duaynlt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgt White Nile: Al Jabalein (protection only)lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtGeographic targeting will focus on centres of gravity, where individuals naturally converge (health and nutrition facilities, IDP settlements and surrounding catchment areas). This approach enables rapid, high-impact assistance where needs are most acute and referral pathways are active, to reach the most vulnerable across all population groups (host communities, returnees, refugees and internally displaced persons), with targeting based on vulnerability rather than status.ltbrgtActed will deliver multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) in line with Cash Working Group guidance on targeting and transfer values. Beneficiaries will be identified through vulnerability criteria linked to acute food insecurity, displacement, returns, protection risks and other shocks, complemented by referral pathways from health and nutrition actors to reach households experiencing poor nutrition or health outcomes not covered by existing assistance. Cash assistance will enable HHs to meet basic needs in a dignified manner, stabilize food consumption, reduce negative coping strategies and support access to essential services, including health and nutrition care. Delivery modalities and transfer values will be informed by market monitoring to ensure feasibility, adequacy and mitigation of inflation-related risks. Partners will support on pre-registration, community outreach, complaints and feedback management, and crowd control.ltbrgtRecognizing that this conflict is first and foremost a protection crisis, Acted will also deliver protection services to reduce risks faced by conflict-affected populations, and to support improved outcomes for these groups. Acted’s protection interventions will focus on support for survivors of sexual violence, separated and unaccompanied children, women, persons with disabilities, and older persons. Community-based protection networks (CBPNs) and staffed protection desks at registration and distribution sites, will support identification and referral of vulnerable populations for case management and, where appropriate individual protection assistance (IPA). ltbrgtTrained caseworkers will deliver confidential protection case management, and for individuals facing acute risks and limited coping capacity, provide IPA as one-off cash or in-kind support to address immediate protection risks and enable access to essential services or safety measures. Protection actors will also work with MPCA teams to ensure protection risks and vulnerabilities inform targeting, referrals and safe assistance delivery. Depending on the state, national NGO partners are expected to support in the creation and training of the CBPNs, set up and management of protection desks and in Gedaref and Gezira, lead on case management and, where appropriate, IPA.ltbrgtActed will coordinate closely with relevant clusters and working groups (CWG, Protection, CCCM, FSAC, Health, Nutrition) and other implementing partners to ensure harmonized and consistent implementation. Where other actors are implementing MPCA (Al Jazirah, Blue Nile, East Darfur) in same localities, Acted will coordinate with partners to agree on caseload allocation, geographic coverage and data sharing to avoid duplication and double targeting at household level. In Gedaref, where WFP will implement Cash for Food (CFF), Acted will coordinate with the CWG, FSL Cluster and WFP to align targeting and share beneficiary lists to ensure complementarity. Assistance will be sequenced where relevant, with MPCA delivered first and CFF in subsequent months to avoid concurrent support.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Multi-sectoral Lifesaving Assistance for the Most Vulnerable People in South Kordofan, North Darfur, West Darfur, Central Darfur and South Darfur, Sud

description.narrative: ltpgtThis proposed project addresses the urgent humanitarian needs of approximately 90,746nbspof the most vulnerable individuals – including 50,643nbspwomen and 40,103nbspmen – across South Kordofan, North Darfur, West Darfur, Central Darfur, and South Darfur, Sudan. The primary focus is on populations in areas classified as inter-sectoral severity 4 and 5, with internally displaced persons (IDPs) comprising 75% of beneficiaries. ltbrgtltbrgtThe project will deliver an integrated and multisectoral response that combines multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA), targeted protection interventions, and emergency shelter support. About 6,592nbspnewly displaced or shock-affected households in South Kordofan will receive one-off emergency MPCA to meet their immediate basic needs, while 7,230nbspprotracted displaced households across the Darfur states will benefit from regular MPCA over three months to support their essential needs and promote household stabilization. Protection activities are designed to ensure that individuals with heightened vulnerabilities have access to safe and effective referral pathways and can receive individualized cash support to address acute protection risks. In North Darfur, the project will also facilitate emergency shelter for 1,500 conflict-affected households through conditional cash assistance, empowering families to secure essential construction materials locally and rebuild safe living environments. ltbrgtltbrgtAll cash-based interventions are rooted in principles of accountability, flexibility, and market sensitivity, ensuring that assistance remains relevant as conditions evolve. NRC and its established Sudanese partners – Alsalam Organization for Rehabilitation and Development (AORD), Nuba Relief, Rehabilitation and Development Organisation (NRRDO) and Hope and Friendship for Development Organization (HOPE) – will leverage their deep local knowledge and trusted community relationships to ensure culturally appropriate, accessible, and effective delivery. These partnerships underpin a commitment to localization and adaptive programming, enhancing the project’s ability to respond to shifting needs and supporting the longer-term resilience of local actors. ltbrgtltbrgtStrong accountability mechanisms and robust monitoring and evaluation (ME) framework are embedded throughout the project cycle. NRC and its partners will ensure that feedback and complaints mechanisms are accessible to all beneficiaries, with regular consultations and participatory approaches informing project design and delivery. The project will implement real-time monitoring, periodic assessments, and systematic data collection to track progress against indicators, ensure transparency, and enable adaptive management. Lessons learned and beneficiary feedback will be used to continually refine interventions, uphold high standards of accountability, and maximize the project’s effectiveness and impact. ltbrgtltbrgtBy delivering rapid, coordinated, and contextually tailored assistance, the project not only addresses immediate needs but also strengthens local capacities and systems, laying the groundwork for a more sustainable humanitarian impact.lt/pgt

title.narrative: Strengthening the WASH Core Pipeline to rapidly provide WASH services and supplies to crisis affected populations across Darfur and West Kordofan

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSolidarités International (SI) will expand the existing WASH Core Pipeline in Darfur and West Kordofan by providing specialized WASH supplies (2nd line essential WASH supplies) to humanitarian actors across Darfur and West Kordofans, strengthening warehousing and stock management, and supporting last-mile delivery. This will ensure actors have timely and equitable access to quality-assured essential WASH supplies for rapid responses to crises, disease outbreaks, and displacements. ltbrgtThe pipeline will prioritize specialized second-line WASH supplies required for rapid rehabilitation, repair and restoration of non-functional or partially functional water-supply systems, complementing UNICEF-managed first-line emergency commodities. ltbrgtThe pipeline is expected to support WASH interventions reaching approximately 500,000 crisis-affected people through Activity 1.1.1 (C-CA1): provision, distribution and replenishment of quick-turnover emergency stockpiles. This includes warehousing and stock management, strategic pre-positioning and replenishment, specialized second-line water-supply rehabilitation and OM materials, and agreed last-mile transport. Through close coordination with the WASH Cluster and UNICEF, SI will pre-position, manage and replenish Core Pipeline stocks in strategic hubs. SI procurement will focus on specialized second-line water-supply materials and components that complement UNICEF-managed first-line emergency commodities, including handpump components, consumable borehole-completion materials, pumps, solar and electrical components, pipes and fittings, tanks and other repair/OM supplies needed for the rapid restoration of essential water supply services. Procurement will be phased during the 11-month implementation period rather than undertaken as a single upfront purchase, allowing quantities, specifications and stock composition to be adjusted to validated partner demand, consumption rates, response priorities, market availability and technical requirements. These items will be held as pipeline stock and released to humanitarian partners against validated needs assessments and requests based on identified needs, response gaps, emergency priorities and available stock. SI will maintain stock visibility and traceability and support eligible last-mile transport in line with the agreed core pipeline specific procedures and arrangements. Receiving partners will report on items distributed and installed, intervention locations and people reached, while SI will conduct risk-based monitoring and spot checks to verify reported results. By reducing procurement lead times and improving access to pre-positioned specialized supplies, the project will enable faster and more coordinated WASH second line responses. ltbrgtTo monitor the use of released supplies, receiving partners will report on items used, intervention locations, and people reached, and SI will conduct risk-based monitoring visits and spot checks to independently verify partner-reported results. PDM or post-intervention checks will be used where relevant to the type of assistance provided.ltbrgtBy reducing procurement lead times, improving access to pre-positioned stocks, strengthening warehousing and stock management, and supporting last-mile delivery, the project will strengthen the operational capacity of national and international humanitarian actors and enable faster, more coordinated responses.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Emergency Pipeline Support in Sudan II

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project will reduce crisis-related morbidity and mortality by sustaining uninterrupted food assistance in severity 4 and 5, underserved areas of North Darfur, including Dar Es Salaam, Melit and Tawila. In parallel, CRS will support Primary Health Care (PHC) medical supply pipelines serving OCHA-prioritized localities across all Darfur states and West Kordofan. Aligned with the Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Envelope 1 focus on urgent core pipeline support, CRS will help prevent breaks in life-saving assistance through time-critical procurement, warehousing, transport and last-mile delivery of food and essential PHC commodities to 885,147 [OM2.1][EE2.2]people among vulnerable internally displaced persons (IDPs), host communities and crisis-affected households.ltbrgtCRS will support the food pipeline by procuring, positioning and delivering in-kind food assistance to an estimated 191,615 crisis-affected people in targeted localities, with attention to households caring for unaccompanied and separated children, complementing wider WFP coverage and filling identified gaps where pipeline disruption would further erode household food security. Geographic and beneficiary prioritization has been coordinated through the Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) Cluster, WFP and relevant coordination mechanisms to avoid duplication and maximize coverage. Under the health component, CRS will establish and manage a common PHC medical supply pipeline, procuring a six months’ supply of a standardized list of essential medical supplies and supporting warehousing, inventory management and dispatch to approximately 161 [OM3.1][AF3.2]health facilities serving an estimated 693,532 [OM4.1][EE4.2]people. This support will preserve delivery capacity established under previous SHF allocations and reduce the risk of stock-outs that could interrupt access to essential primary health care in areas where health systems have been severely weakened by conflict, displacement and disease outbreaks.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtFood commodities will be sourced through regional channels via Chad and routed through Abéché as the main food commodity hub before onward delivery into North Darfur. Essential medical supplies will be procured through international procurement channels and routed through health supply hubs in Ed Daein, Zalingei and Tawila, in line with the locations identified for the PHC pipeline. Both pipelines will use a flexible hub-and-spoke logistics model, with routing and dispatch schedules adjusted as needed in response to access conditions. CRS will leverage established procurement systems, supplier relationships, cross-border logistics capacity and Primary Distribution Point (PDP – for food commodities) [HA5.1]in Abeche, Chad contingency storage near the border and inside Sudan (Adre, Geneina), and onward transport to delivery points in North Darfur.ltbrgtConsistent with SHF localization commitments, CRS will contract with Aid Point, a Sudanese organization, through a Service Agreement to lead implementation in Dar Es Salaam and Melit for the food commodities component. [CA6.1]CRS will also provide targeted capacity strengthening and accompaniment to local partners in areas such as commodity management, accountability to affected populations (AAP), protection mainstreaming, monitoring, and compliance with SHF requirements. CRS will manage procurement, warehousing, and transport to the food Primary Distribution Point (PDP) in Abéché, and onward movement to the relevant Final Distribution Points (FDPs). For Dar Es Salaam and Melit, the selected local service provider will manage last-mile distribution to target communities. For Tawila, Aid Point will collect food commodities from the Tawila FDP for onward distribution to IDP camps.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Rapid Life-Saving Shelter/NFI, Cash and Protection Assistance in Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtSince April 2023, Sudan has faced one of the largest and most complex humanitarian crises globally. Armed conflict, mass displacement, the collapse of essential services and severe access constraints have pushed millions into acute need, with hyper-prioritized inter-sector severity 4 and 5 localities experiencing catastrophic humanitarian conditions. In line with the US Fast-Track Reserve Allocation Strategy, UNHCR will implement a six-month response to scale up life-saving assistance in selected high-severity areas.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe intervention will be delivered through a partnership model that prioritizes localization and operational reach. UNHCR will work with nine implementing partners, including five national NGOs that play a critical role in community engagement, protection activities and last-mile distribution of emergency relief items. UNHCR will also engage closely with IDP- and refugee-led organizations and communities through community-based protection networks. Through these partnerships and close coordination with other humanitarian actors, UNHCR aims to maximize the protection outcomes of the response while enabling rapid delivery of assistance.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUNHCR will implement a three-pillar intervention:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt1) Emergency Shelter and NFIs PipelineltbrgtUNHCR will provide emergency shelter support to 4,000 households (ca. 20,000 individuals) and distribute core NFI kits to 23,450 households (ca. 137,250 individuals) in hyper-prioritized localities, including the Darfur and Kordofan States. Through international and local procurement, pre-positioning and flexible last-mile delivery arrangements, the intervention will enable crisis-affected households to access safe shelter, reduce exposure to harsh weather conditions and meet urgent basic needs.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt2) Life-Saving Protection Assistancelt/pgtltpgtUNHCR will provide life-saving protection assistance to 39,428 individuals facing acute protection risks. Individuals identified will receive targeted protection responses, including case management, child protection interventions and response to conflict-related violence, as well as emergency protection cash assistance through Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) to address urgent safety and protection needs. Protection assistance will also include the provision of dignity kits for women and girls and mobility aids for persons with disabilities to support safe access to services. Where needed and possible, individuals will be referred to multisectoral life-saving services and assistance. Protection actions will be delivered in close coordination with shelter, NFI and cash responses to help open protection space and ensure that urgent needs are addressed in an integrated manner.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt3) Multi-Purpose Cash AssistanceltbrgtUNHCR will deliver multi-purpose cash assistance to 7,200 households (ca. 36,000 individuals), in complementarity with other interventions and in coordination with Cash WG. Cash assistance will enable vulnerable households to meet urgent basic needs in a dignified manner and reduce exposure to life-threatening coping strategies, complementing the provision of in-kind emergency assistance.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTogether, these interventions will provide rapid, life-saving support to crisis-affected populations in some of the most severely affected areas of Sudan, while leveraging partnerships with national organizations to strengthen localized response and ensure timely delivery of assistance.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Procurement and distribution of health, nutrition and WASH supplies to reach the most vulnerable children and families in 84 hyper-prioritized localities in Sudan with lifesaving assistance.

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtSudan is facing one of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises - escalating violence, mass displacement, food insecurity, disease outbreaks and the collapse of essential services have pushed millions to the brink, including 17.3 million children who are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance. The health system is at near total collapse, with 70 per cent of facilities nonfunctional, leaving 3.4 million children under five at risk of deadly diseases. One in three people lacks safe water, and a water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) crisis is affecting 28 million people and fueling outbreaks. The country continues to face a severe crisis in nutrition and food security, with nearly 40 percent of the population food insecure. In 2026, an estimated 3.6 million children under five are projected to suffer from acute malnutrition, including about 825,000 with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM). Famine has already been declared in several localities, and the October 2025 IPC analysis confirmed famine has persisted in two areas with 20 additional areas across Darfur and Kordofan at high risk.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThis project focuses on the procurement and distribution of lifesaving health, nutrition and WASH supplies across the 84 hyper-prioritized localities (severity 4 and 5) in Sudan.ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtThe health component of this project aims to reach 2.1 million children and families through the delivery of essential health supplies (e.g., IEHK, AWD/cholera kits, and midwifery and newborn care kits) in conflict-affected and hard-to-reach areas where health system functionality has been severely disrupted, disease outbreak risks remain high, and vulnerable populations face significant barriers to accessing essential health services. Critical supplies will be delivered to UNICEF-supported health facilities and/or mobile teams, restoring access to essential health services to reduce excess mortality through improved outbreak readiness and rapid response, ensuring safe delivery and emergency maternal and newborn care, and maintaining access to essential medicines for children and other vulnerable groups.nbsplt/ligtltligtThe nutrition component aims to reach 100,000 children with lifesaving treatment for SAM across hyper-prioritized localities, which collectively represent half of the national SAM burden. As the sole provider of therapeutic supplies for SAM treatment in Sudan, UNICEF, through this project, will ensure the availability of Ready to Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF), covering 54 percent of the six-month requirement.nbspDistribution of RUTF will be guided by caseload, consumption, and admission trends.lt/ligtltligtThe WASH component aims to reachnbspltspangt1.3 millionlt/spangtltspangt people with access to safe water through procurement and distribution of lifesaving WASH supplies (e.g., water treatment chemicals, soaps, household water storage items, emergency latrine materials).lt/spangtlt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtUNICEF will manage the procurement of supplies (local and offshore), in-country transportation, warehousing, and last-mile delivery, includingnbspto health facilities and mobile teams in hard-to-reach areas. Overall, the project will strengthen health, nutrition and WASH supply chain and ensure uninterrupted access to lifesaving assistance for vulnerable children and families.nbspltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtJoint planning with existing coordination mechanismsnbspwill enhance transportation efficiency, storage optimization, and last-mile delivery.nbsplt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtProtection remains an integral part of this project, with safety audits, female staff presence, accessible information tools, and tailored supplies to reduce conflict-related sexual violence risks and ensure dignified access for people with disabilities and other at-risk groups.lt/pgt

title.narrative: Emergency Multisectoral Assistance for Newly Displaced and Vulnerable Populations in Hyper-Prioritized High-Risk Conflict Areas

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe project provides rapid, life-saving assistance to crisis-affected populations in the 84 hyper-prioritized severity 4–5 localities identified by the UN and SHF across Sudan, where conflict has generated acute unmet needs and severely reduced coping capacities as well as areas that could fall within the same classification during the timeline of the project. Through the IOM Common Pipeline, the intervention will procure, pre-position, and deliver family tents, NFI and hygiene kits through pipeline partners to 74,000 households based on verified needs and cluster coordination. All lifesaving services will be delivered in a safe, accountable and participatory manner.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Scaling up security support to enable essential UN programme delivery and protection activities in North Darfur and the Kordofans

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project will be implemented by the United Nations Department of Safety and Security to support humanitarian operations across Darfur and the Kordofans in Sudan, with a particular focus on North Darfur—especially Tawila locality—and other high-priority areas in the Kordofan regions. Recognizing security as a critical enabling function across all clusters, the project aims to facilitate humanitarian access, protection, and life-saving activities at acceptable levels of risk.ltbrgtltbrgtThe project will directly support UN agencies and humanitarian partners by deploying dedicated front-line personnel, establishing secure communications systems, and strengthening security analysis and information-sharing. A central objective is to enhance the ability of humanitarian actors to operate safely while delivering timely and effective assistance in complex and high-risk environments.ltbrgtltbrgtImplementation will be carried out through field-based teams under the management of UNDSS at the country level, in close coordination with humanitarian partners. The project is designed to support the formal coordination system, particularly inter-sectoral mechanisms, and is structured around three main pillars:ltbrgtltbrgt1.Information Gathering and Security Analysis: This pillar focuses on collecting and analysing field-level data on the access constraints and security risks. Through a strengthened Security Information and Operations Cell, the project will produce timely, actionable analysis to inform operational decision-making. This includes information on potential threats to civilians, gender-specific risks, and risks affecting front-line humanitarian actors. The information will be systematically shared with humanitarian actors to support risk-informed programming, strengthen mitigation measures, and enhance overall response effectiveness.ltbrgtltbrgt2. Community Engagement: Field teams will engage directly with affected communities to strengthen the relevance, accountability, and safety of the humanitarian response. This includes facilitating dialogue between communities, humanitarian actors, and other stakeholders andnbspgathering feedback on risks and response gaps. Community engagement will also help monitor local conflict dynamics and identify aspects that can affect aid workers, including gender-based risks and protection of civilians.ltbrgtltbrgt3. Service Coordination: The project will support the inter-agency coordination and communication between United Nations agencies, funds and programmes and international and national non-governmental organizations under the Saving Lives Together framework. This will contribute to streamlining humanitarian services across Darfur and the Kordofans, and improve the overall safety coordination.ltbrgtltbrgtIn addition, the project will work closely with United Nations Agencies, relevant authorities, and coordination structures to facilitate humanitarian access, including efforts to establish and maintain safe corridors for aid delivery. Strong collaboration will be ensured with the Access Working Group to align security analysis with operational and humanitarian priorities. Through improved coordination and analysis, the project will contribute to safer, more effective delivery of assistance to vulnerable populations.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project builds on established approaches in field-based information gathering, security coordination, and community engagement in complex emergencies. Existing mechanisms for sharing data and analysis will be further strengthened to support timely decision-making and targeted response. The enhanced focus on security as an enabling function, combined with improved coordination and information systems, will ensure that humanitarian actors are better equipped to operate safely and effectively in Sudan’s most challenging environments.ltbrgtlt/pgtnbspnbspnbspnbspnbspnbsp

title.narrative: Emergency Food Assistance and Common Logistics Services for Highly Food-Insecure Communities in Hyper-Prioritized Inter-Cluster Priority Localities

description.narrative: ltpgtltugtGeneral Food Assistancelt/ugtltbrgtThis project will deliver life-saving General Food Assistance (GFA) to severely food-insecure populations in hyper-prioritized inter-cluster localities, in line with inter-agency severity analysis and the 2026 Strategy and Prioritization Framework of WFP Sudan.ltbrgtThe intervention is designed to maintain continuity of assistance during a period of anticipated pipeline constraints by combining cash-based transfers (CBT) and in-kind food assistance. With this contribution, WFP will be able to bridge critical pipeline gaps and ensure sustained assistance to the most vulnerable households while adapting to rapidly changing operational conditions.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtBeneficiary planning figures presented in this proposal are scenario-driven, with risk-informed assumptions. These assumptions are utilized to illustrate the maximum feasible scale of coverage achievable within the available funding envelope, while preserving operational flexibility to respond to evolving needs, in view of access conditions, market functionality, and funding and commodity pipelines across the 84 prioritized locations.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe funding envelope corresponds to an indicative provision of total in-kind food assistance of 16,847.5 mt to reach an estimated 1,179,797 people. Further, the project aims to provide monthly cash assistance for an estimated 674,479 people through CBT sub-modalities—Digital Cash Transfers (DCT), Cash-in-Hand (CiH), and Value Vouchers (VV), where market conditions and operational feasibility allow. Through this approach, the project will stabilize food consumption, reduce acute hunger, and maximize the impact of limited resources during a critical phase of the response.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTransfer values (and any potential changes) for CBT will align with the Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) cluster guidance the FSL cluster is responsible for setting and coordinating cash-for-food (sectoral cash) transfer values, in coordination with the interagency Cash Working Group.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltugtLogistics Clusterlt/ugtltbrgtSince the onset of the war in April 2023, humanitarian operations have faced several challenges, including sporadic movement restrictions, airspace closures, limited access, complex deconfliction processes, bureaucratic and administrative impediments, rising transport and storage costs, and disrupted telecommunications infrastructure. Depending on evolving conflict dynamics, some of supply routes as well as cross-border and crossline access get disrupted, and storage capacity is limited. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTo address critical logistics constraints, the Logistics Cluster (LC) continues to scale up its activities, with its Concept of Operations guided by the annual Gaps and Needs Analysis. From Port Sudan, it leads national and sub-national coordination, information management and common services. Free-to-user common storage is provided in Ad Dabbah, Gedaref, Kassala, Kosti, Port Sudan, and Tawila, with further expansion planned in Khartoum and El Obeid based on needs. Transport is provided strictly on a last-resort basis. ltbrgtThe Cluster will facilitate inter-agency crossline convoys using common transport services to priority areas in Darfur and Kordofan states, with dedicated staff and using established coordination and information management functions. The LC will support consolidation and prepositioning of supplies at key hubs and establish a new common storage facility in El Obeid, enabling the strategic positioning of supplies closer to priority locations in the Kordofan region. Support will focus on priority localities identified by the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG). WFP, through the LC, has been also tasked with establishing enhanced monitoring of UN consignments entering Sudan via the Adré crossing from Chad, reinforcing UN risk management systems by verifying the humanitarian nature of cargo. The team will be embedded within the LC, reporting to the Sudan RC/HC and regularly updating the Chad RC/HC, while coordinating with UN agencies.lt/pgt

title.narrative: Saving Lives and Protecting Livelihoods through Livestock Vaccinations in Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project intends to provide critical life saving support to vulnerable households in 70 locations within Darfur and Kordofan and four localities in Khartoum through the provision of livestock vaccination. Livestock products are critical in enabling the maintenance of a diversified diet in rural communities in target locations and in supporting both household transport and agricultural production. lt/pgtltpgtObjective: To save lives and protect the food security, nutrition and productive assets of conflict-affected and vulnerable populations in Sudan through emergency livestock vaccination.lt/pgtltpgtNeeds: According to the latest population in need figures (PIN) produced by the Inter Cluster Coordination Group in Sudan, over 16 million people are in need of assistance in Sudan, with 9.3 million people in Darfur and Kordofan in severity levels 4 and 5. The needs in Darfur and Kordofan are driven by large scale displacement and the decimation of livelihoods, with the Famine Review Committee noting the targeted destruction of markets, water points and health centres and the movement of people from their homes into the bush (IPC snapshot May 2026). In these situations livestock are often the only remaining productive asset available to families and represent an essential source of both food and transport. However, despite high numbers (Darfur and Kordofan collectively host 59.5% of the national herd (CFSAM 2025), low vaccination figures (just 5% of animals in the two regions have been vaccinated since the start of the war) mean that the risk of both transboundary (e.g. Contagious Bovine and Caprine Pleuropneumonia) and zoonotic diseases (e.g. Anthrax and Rabies) is significant. Protecting animals from these diseases is therefore of critical importance in both reducing the incidence of life-threatening diseases and enabling communities to maintain access to healthy and varied protein rich animal-based diets. Both of these benefits serve to relieve pressure on fragile primary health care facilities. Given the importance of donkeys in assisting women to transport water and in assisting people to access markets (including women, older people and people with disabilities), vaccination against African Horse Sickness (reported in both Darfur and Kordofan) has been included in the project. In addition, the project has deliberately been designed to include the vaccination of small stock (e.g. goats, sheeps), which are more commonly owned by women than cattle or camels and, due to their ability to survive of browse as well as grass, are able to remain closer to homesteads, providing a readily available source of milk for women and children.lt/pgtltpgtTargeting and Response: The proposed intervention will target 1.25 million people in 70 locations in severity level 4 and 5 across both Darfur and Kordofan. Four additional localities in Khartoum have been included in this proposal due in part to the food security severity index (all are in levels 4), but also because Khartoum represents a critical market for livestock products moving up from other parts of the country. This means that livestock keepers in Khartoum are disproportionately exposed to both transboundary and zoonotic livestock diseases. Forty percent of beneficiaries will be drawn from IDP and returnee families with the remaining 60 percent drawn from host communities. To kick start the vaccination process, FAO will utilise existing stocks of vaccine (stored in West Darfur and Port Sudan) these will be supplemented (and replenished) by additional vaccines procured through the project.lt/pgt

title.narrative: Emergency Food Assistance for Highly Food-Insecure Communities in Hyper-Prioritized Inter-Cluster Priority Localities - Tranche 2

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project will deliver life‑saving General Food Assistance (GFA) to severely food‑insecure populations in hyper‑prioritized inter-cluster localities, in line with inter‑agency severity analysis and the 2026 Strategy and Prioritization Framework of WFP Sudan. These assumptions are utilized to illustrate the maximum feasible scale of coverage achievable within the available funding envelope, while preserving operational flexibility to respond to evolving needs, in view of access conditions, market functionality, and funding and commodity pipelines across the 97 prioritized locations.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe funding envelope corresponds to an indicative provision of monthly in-kind food assistance of 13,152 mt to reach an estimated 636,161 people. Currently, WFP plans to use the in-kind portion of this funding for local procurement of Sorghum.ltbrgtFurther, the project aims to provide monthly cash assistance for an estimated 1,000,032 people through CBT sub‑modalities of Digital Cash Transfers (DCT), Cash-in-Hand (CiH), and Value Vouchers (VV), where market conditions and operational feasibility allow.
