This enabled WFP to address longstanding logistical and access challenges that had often prevented vulnerable populations from receiving timely food assistance due to insecurity and supply chain constraints.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe Darfur experience has demonstrated that cash assistance can be effectively delivered at scale in highly fragile environments when supported by robust market monitoring, phased implementation, strong community engagement, protection safeguards, and adaptive risk management measures. Building on these lessons, WFP will continue to prioritise CBT in these areas while further strengthening programme quality and accountability. Particular attention will be given to enhancing retailer price monitoring and exploring additional delivery mechanisms, including digital cash transfers where feasible and appropriate.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe new tranche will also support the expansion of CBT operations into South Kordofan, enabling continued assistance in areas where logistical constraints remain significant. In the past, due to access limitations, beneficiaries in some locations were enrolled through self-registration processes. With improved access now available, WFP plans to conduct physical verification of registered beneficiaries to strengthen assurance measures, validate eligibility, and ensure that assistance is provided to verified households in a transparent and accountable manner.lt/pgt

reporting-org.narrative: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title.narrative: ILSS — Integrated Life-Saving Supplies: Cholera Prevention and WASH Response in Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtSudan remains one of the world’s most severe and complex humanitarian crises, with conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks and disruption of basic services driving critical Health and WASH needs. Reliable core supply pipelines are essential to sustaining life-saving services and enabling rapid response to acute needs, including cholera and other public health emergencies, particularly in areas facing high humanitarian severity and constrained access. Under the Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF) 2026 Fourth Reserve Allocation (RA4) – “Sustaining Core Pipelines and Enabling Services through the Second US Contribution to the Sudan Humanitarian Fund” – UNICEF will deliver US$21 million in life-saving Health and WASH core pipeline supplies. Over 12 months, supplies will be prioritised based on vulnerability, disease and outbreak risks, service gaps, displacement, access and evolving operational conditions, maintaining an agile and conflict-sensitive approach.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUnder the WASH component (US$13 million 62 per cent), UNICEF will procure, pre-position and distribute essential WASH supplies, including water treatment chemicals, household water treatment and storage items, soap, sanitation supplies and emergency water equipment. These commodities will sustain access to safe water and WASH services and support prevention and response to cholera and other waterborne diseases. Pipeline planning, stock, distribution and coverage information will be coordinated and shared through national and sub-national WASH Cluster mechanisms to support collective gap analysis, prioritisation and complementarity with other SHF-funded pipeline actors, including Solidarités International in Darfur, and avoid duplication. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUnder the Health component (US$8 million 38 per cent), UNICEF will procure essential medicines and emergency health supplies, including AWD/cholera kits, Interagency Emergency Health Kit (IEHK) components and supplementary modules, IMCI medicines, and maternal and newborn health supplies. IEHK supplies procured under the project will be available to eligible Health Cluster partners based on identified needs and priorities, rather than limited to UNICEF-supported partners. Allocation, distribution tracking and reporting will be coordinated through the Health Cluster Medical Supplies and Logistics Working Group (MSL WG), using agreed MSL WG tools and processes to promote transparent and equitable access, priority-based allocation, pipeline visibility and timely and complete reporting. This approach will also strengthen collective monitoring of stock levels and emerging gaps and reduce the risk of stockouts across Health Cluster partners. ltbrgtUNICEF will build on its established procurement, warehousing and in-country distribution capacity to manage commodities from procurement through last-mile delivery. Supplies will be strategically positioned and allocated according to needs, consumption, pipeline status and access conditions, with procurement and distribution schedules regularly adapted to supply arrivals and evolving humanitarian priorities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtMonitoring will combine supply and distribution tracking, field monitoring, post-distribution and end-use monitoring, spot checks and third-party verification where required. UNICEF will track supply receipt, use and gaps to enable corrective action, complemented by community feedback. Health supply monitoring and reporting will use agreed MSL WG tools to strengthen Cluster-wide visibility and accountability. UNICEF will report through OneGMS and share key findings and risks with OCHA/HFU and AIT to support timely course correction and accountable use of SHF resources.ltbrgtlt/pgt

reporting-org.narrative: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title.narrative: Integrated WASH in Health Response to Reduce Morbidity and Mortality in Khartoum and North Darfur States

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtKhartoum State remains at high risk of cholera, acute watery diarrhoea (AWD), hepatitis E and vector-borne disease outbreaks due to conflict-related damage to water and sanitation infrastructure, inadequate waste management, electricity disruptions, and the return of displaced populations to heavily damaged urban areas. In Jebel Awlia, Karrari and Omdurman localities, health facilities and surrounding communities face critical gaps in access to safe water, sanitation, healthcare waste management, infection prevention and control (IPC), and outbreak preparedness.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtIn North Darfur, Tawila locality hosted an estimated 570,000 IDPs in Tawila Omda Camps A, B and C and Daba Naira Camps A and B as of July 2026. Severe operational and capacity constraints continue to limit the delivery of essential WASH services. Following the cholera outbreak of June–December 2025, overcrowding, poor sanitation and limited access to safe water have heightened health risks, particularly ahead of the 2026 rainy season. In both states, these conditions increase morbidity and mortality risks and undermine the continuity of essential health services.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThrough this project, Solidarités International (SI), in partnership with Sudan Zero Waste Organization (SZWO) and Blue Society Voluntary Organization (BSVO), will implement an integrated WASH and cholera response in high-risk areas of Khartoum and North Darfur. The intervention combines emergency service delivery, rehabilitation of critical WASH infrastructure, outbreak preparedness and rapid response to reduce disease transmission and improve access to lifesaving services.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn Tawila, SI will provide safe water to IDP populations through emergency water trucking. Given the extensive conflict-related damage to WASH infrastructure, urgent water supply assistance is required to meet immediate needs and mitigate cholera transmission risks.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn Khartoum, the project will strengthen WASH services in targeted health facilities through WASH FIT assessments and improvement planning, rehabilitation of sanitation facilities and water infrastructure, construction of handwashing stations, provision of IPC supplies, healthcare waste management support, water quality monitoring, and emergency desludging. Strategic water systems serving health facilities and surrounding communities will be rehabilitated and solarized, while Water User Committees will be supported to strengthen operation and maintenance capacities.ltbrgtAt community level, the consortium will implement hygiene promotion and risk communication activities, environmental sanitation campaigns, vector control interventions, water quality monitoring and treatment, borehole mapping, and community capacity-strengthening initiatives. These activities will target outbreak-prone areas and promote safe hygiene practices, environmental health and community ownership of WASH services.ltbrgtTo strengthen preparedness and response to cholera, AWD and hepatitis E outbreaks, the project will establish facility-level rapid response mechanisms, conduct transmission analysis and hotspot mapping, train and equip Rapid Response Teams and Community-Led CATI teams, support emergency water treatment and monitoring, implement targeted RCCE activities, distribute cholera and WASH kits, provide emergency IPC support to health facilities, and conduct ring-response interventions around reported cases in coordination with the State Ministry of Health and Health Cluster partners. The project will also support the pilot operation of mobile water treatment units procured through a separate funding mechanism to ensure rapid access to safe drinking water during outbreaks.ltbrgtImplemented in coordination with government institutions and Cluster partners, the project will strengthen local capacities, support localization, increase resilience and contribute to reducing preventable morbidity and mortality while improving public health conditions in vulnerable areas of Sudan.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Relief International Reducing Preventable Morbidity and Mortality through Integrated Life-Saving Health and Nutrition Services Localized Humanitarian Action in North Darfur and Northern state, Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality among conflict‑affected populations, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and vulnerable host communities in high‑ and very high‑severity localities across North Darfur and Northern State through an integrated Health and Nutrition response. The project is firmly anchored in the SHF localization agenda and will be delivered through a consortium comprising three national NGOs. National partners APD, SHPDO, and JPRD will manage approximately 35% of the budget and lead implementation across multiple localities, leveraging their community acceptance, contextual knowledge, and operational access. RI will provide technical accompaniment, partnership support, compliance oversight, and capacity strengthening through mentoring, joint monitoring, and embedded technical support. The project will strengthen local leadership and institutional capacity while delivering lifesaving assistance. ltbrgtHealth interventions will support 23 primary healthcare facilities and 1 secondary healthcare facility, restoring access to essential primary and secondary healthcare services, maternal and newborn health services, emergency and trauma care, immunization, mental health and psychosocial support, referral systems, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness, and response services. The project aims to deliver 144,659 outpatient consultations, support 2,976 assisted deliveries, provide at least two ANC visits to 2,430 pregnant women, facilitate 145 referrals for specialized care, and strengthen disease surveillance and outbreak response systems. Community health workers and local partner networks will support health promotion, community-based surveillance, referrals, and risk communication. ltbrgtNutrition interventions will focus on North Darfur through a partnership model involving RI, APD, SHPDO and JPRD. The project will support 29 OTP/TSFP sites providing Community-Based Management of Acute Malnutrition services, including treatment, IYCF counselling, referral to Stabilization Centres, community-based screening, and integrated nutrition campaigns. The intervention will admit 5,438 children with SAM and 740 pregnant and lactating women with acute malnutrition for treatment, screen more than 40,288 individuals for acute malnutrition, and provide MYCN counselling to 17,670 caregivers and pregnant women. It will also establish 24 MSGs train 174 health workers and 120 Community Nutrition Volunteers to strengthen community-based nutrition systems and local capacity. ltbrgtAcross all sectors, the project will integrate accountability to affected populations, protection mainstreaming, PSEA, gender/disability inclusion, and community feedback mechanisms. Through national partner leadership, community engagement, and targeted capacity strengthening, the project will deliver lifesaving services while advancing locally led humanitarian action and strengthening sustainable response capacity in some of Sudan's most vulnerable communities. ltbrgt lt/pgt

title.narrative: Integrated Health, Nutrition, and Protection-Centered Response to Reduce Preventable Morbidity and Mortality among Crisis-Affected Populations

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSudan's humanitarian crisis continues to drive large-scale displacement, disease outbreaks, acute malnutrition and disruption of essential health services. North Darfur remains among the worst-affected states following the destruction of Zamzam Camp and the escalation of conflict in El Fasher, resulting in repeated displacement of vulnerable populations to Tawila and surrounding areas. The continued influx of internally displaced persons has placed exceptional pressure on already overstretched health and nutrition services, creating urgent needs for sustained access to life-saving care.ltbrgtALIMA proposes a 12-month integrated Primary Health Care (PHC) and Nutrition project from 1 August 2026 to 31 July 2027 in El Fasher and Tawila localities, North Darfur, with a total budget of USD 1,250,000 (USD 800,000 for Health and USD 450,000 for Nutrition). The intervention will support Garni PHCC in El Fasher locality and Katur PHCC, Marta, Kongnia, Umda East Gate and Salab Laba mobile clinic sites in Tawila locality, ensuring continuity of essential services following the handover of Garni and Katur PHCCs from MSF France and MSF Spain.ltbrgtThe project will deliver a comprehensive PHC package, including outpatient consultations, integrated management of childhood illnesses, management of communicable and non-communicable diseases, sexual and reproductive health, maternal and child health, routine immunization, mental health and psychosocial support, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness, health promotion and referral services. Patients requiring inpatient or specialized care will be referred to the MSF France-supported inpatient facility in El Fasher or ALIMA's Daba Nyara Inpatient Department (IPD) in Tawila, according to established referral pathways.ltbrgtNutrition interventions will include community and facility-based screening, outpatient treatment of uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition (SAM), referral and inpatient management of complicated SAM, infant and young child feeding (IYCF) counselling, and integration of nutrition services within both fixed and mobile PHC services. Essential infection prevention and control (IPC), safe water supply, sanitation and healthcare waste management measures will be maintained within supported health facilities as part of quality service delivery.ltbrgtALIMA will implement the project in partnership with the Peace Organization for Rural Development (PORD) under a sub-grant arrangement that strengthens national leadership. ALIMA will manage the fixed PHCCs, project coordination, technical oversight, referrals, monitoring and reporting. PORD will receive a sub-grant of USD 200,000 to implement PHC and nutrition services through the project's mobile clinics, including outpatient consultations, nutrition screening, treatment of uncomplicated SAM, health promotion, community mobilization and referrals. Distinct activities, targets and budgets will be assigned to each organization, supported through joint supervision, technical mentoring, financial oversight and safeguarding measures.ltbrgtThe project will contribute to SHF priorities by ensuring uninterrupted access to quality PHC and nutrition services for conflict-affected displaced and host populations while strengthening localization through meaningful engagement of a national partner.ltbrgt lt/pgt

title.narrative: Strengthening Integrated Primary and Secondary Paediatric Health and Nutrition Services in South Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality among conflict-affected and vulnerable children in Nyala Shimal, South Darfur, by sustaining access to free, high-quality, life-saving paediatric healthcare and nutrition services. ltbrgtThe paediatric focus responds to the demographic and epidemiological profile of the crisis and constitutes a targeted contribution to essential PHC. Children account for more than half of Sudan’s internally displaced population, while South Darfur hosts the country’s highest proportion of IDPs. Nationally, UNICEF estimated that 3.4 million children under five were at high risk of epidemic diseases due to declining vaccination coverage, damaged health and WASH infrastructure, and deteriorating nutritional conditions. ltbrgtIPC projects Nyala Shimal’s nutrition situation to deteriorate to Phase 4 (Critical) during the June-September 2026 period. This projection is consistent with EMERGENCY (EMR)’s facility data, which show that malnutrition rose from 37% of admissions in January-May 2025 to 64% in the same period of 2026. The increasing severity of cases supports the need to sustain integrated outpatient and inpatient paediatric and nutrition services.ltbrgtThese risks affect children disproportionately. Malaria, respiratory infections, diarrhoeal diseases and measles can progress rapidly, particularly when combined with malnutrition, delayed care-seeking and low vaccination coverage. The intervention therefore complements the wider PHC response by prioritising a population with particularly high vulnerability and unmet need.ltbrgtThrough EMR’s Paediatric Centre in Nyala, the project will sustain one of the few available service points providing a continuum between primary and secondary paediatric care. At primary level, the Centre will deliver outpatient consultations, early diagnosis and treatment, nutrition screening and identification of danger signs. At secondary level, it will provide inpatient care, clinical stabilisation, continuous monitoring and management of severe or complicated conditions, with referral for specialised care when feasible. Integrating both levels in the same facility is essential where referral options and inpatient stabilisation capacity are limited. It enables children to move rapidly from assessment to treatment and admission, reducing delays, interrupted referrals, loss to follow-up and avoidable deterioration.ltbrgtAll consultations, diagnostics, medicines, nutritional treatment and inpatient care will be free of charge, removing financial barriers for displaced and vulnerable families. Quality will be ensured through qualified Sudanese professionals, standardised paediatric protocols, diagnostic capacity, infection prevention and control, reliable medicines and supplies, mentoring and technical supervision.ltbrgtNutrition services will be fully integrated into paediatric care. All children aged 6-59 months will undergo systematic MUAC and weight-for-height screening, irrespective of the reason for consultation. Children identified with MAM or SAM will receive appropriate nutritional and medical management or referral. Follow-up, caregiver counselling and defaulter tracing will support continuity through to recovery.ltbrgtChild protection will be mainstreamed through child-safe, confidential, inclusive and non-discriminatory practices. Local capacity will be reinforced through Sudanese professionals and coordination with the Ministry of Health, the Health and Nutrition Clusters, UN agencies and humanitarian partners.ltbrgtBy preserving integrated primary and secondary paediatric healthcare and nutrition services, the project will address a critical gap within the broader PHC response and protect children whose age, displacement, malnutrition and disease exposure place them at particularly high risk of preventable death.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Reducing Preventable Morbidity Mortality through Integrated, Life-Saving Services Nutrition and Protection-Response in North Kordofan (Sheikan,Um Dam Haj) and South Kordofan(Dilling)

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe proposed project, “Reducing Preventable Morbidity Mortality through Integrated Nutrition and Protection Services,” aims to address critical, life-threatening needs in conflict-affected areas of North Kordofan (Sheikan and Um Dam Haj Ahmed) and South Kordofan (Dilling), Sudan. Implemented over a 10-month period, the intervention responds to the severe deterioration of humanitarian conditions driven by ongoing conflict, displacement, and limited access to essential nutrition and protection services.lt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbgtNutrition activities will be implemented only in Dilling, while Child Protection, GBV and General Protection activities will be implemented in Dilling, Sheikan and Um Dam Haj Ahmed.lt/bgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe targeted localities face acute gaps in access to quality nutrition and protection services, particularly for women, children, and other vulnerable groups. Malnutrition rates remain high due to food insecurity, poor infant and young child feeding practices, displacement, and limited availability of nutrition services. Conflict and population movements have further reduced access to essential nutrition support, placing vulnerable households at increased risk of adverse health and nutritional outcomes.ltbrgtProtection risks are also significant, including exposure to gender-based violence (GBV), child protection concerns, psychological distress, family separation, and limited access to safe and inclusive services. Displacement and insecurity have weakened traditional community protection mechanisms, leaving vulnerable populations with reduced access to support structures, referral pathways, and specialized services.ltbrgtTo address these challenges, the project adopts an integrated approach that combines nutrition and protection interventions, recognizing the close link between nutritional well-being and protection outcomes. Nutrition activities will focus on community-based screening for malnutrition, referral and treatment support for acute malnutrition, promotion of appropriate infant and young child feeding practices, and community awareness activities aimed at improving nutritional outcomes for vulnerable populations.ltbrgtProtection interventions will strengthen community-based protection mechanisms, provide case management and referral services, support child protection and GBV risk mitigation efforts, and facilitate access to safe, inclusive, and dignified services. Particular emphasis will be placed on safeguarding women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups while promoting accountability to affected populations.ltbrgtThe project prioritizes community engagement and local partnerships to enhance acceptance, access, and sustainability. It will work closely with local actors and community structures to ensure culturally appropriate service delivery and strengthen local capacity. Adaptive and flexible implementation modalities, including mobile outreach and community-based approaches where appropriate, will enable continuity of services in a highly volatile and access-constrained environment.ltbrgtOverall, the project aims to reduce preventable morbidity and improve the well-being of conflict-affected populations by expanding access to quality nutrition services while addressing critical protection risks. By targeting the most vulnerable populations in underserved and conflict-affected areas, the intervention will contribute to improved nutritional outcomes, enhanced protection, strengthened community resilience, and more effective community-based systems for service delivery and protection.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Enhancing Health Outcomes through an Integrated Lifesaving WASH and Protection-Centered Response in White Nile and South Kordofan States, Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtSudan faces a severe humanitarian crisis: over 17M people lack safe water, 24M lack adequate sanitation, over 70% of health facilities do not have a reliable water supply, and more than 10M are displaced. The collapse of WASH services is fueling deadly outbreaks of cholera, hepatitis E, and other epidemics—especially in White Nile and South Kordofan—putting millions of lives at immediate risk. ltbrgt ltbrgtThis project is strategically designed to address urgent humanitarian needs by delivering an integrated WASH and protection response in six high-priority localities of White Nile (4) and South Kordofan (2)—selected based on high internally displaced and returnees’ density, critical service gaps, and vulnerability to disease outbreaks. A core focus is strengthening WASH services in health facilities, which are essential for infection prevention and the safe delivery of health and nutrition services. By ensuring reliable access to safe water, sanitation, and effective hygiene within health centers and overcrowded IDP camps, the project will help break the cycle of disease transmission and reduce preventable deaths. The project will also seek to promote positive hygiene behaviors through risk communication and the distribution of essential supplies, ensure WASH services are accessible, equitable, and delivered with dignity, and strengthen the capacity of communities and health facilities to respond to protection risks and public health emergencies. An estimated ltbgt47,449 (F: 26,365 M: 21,084)lt/bgt conflict-affected and displaced people are expected to benefit from this project. ltbrgt ltbrgtIn line with the Sudan’s Protection Cluster’s Guidance Note on Integrated Protection in Health, WASH and Nutrition Responses ltbgt(Annex 14)lt/bgt, NRC will also integrate general protection activities with WASH programming to ensure immediate and sustained improvements in health, safety, and dignity—especially in health facilities and IDP camps where risks are acute in White Nile. By pairing WASH interventions with targeted protection measures, the project will ensure that HFs, water points, sanitation facilities, and hygiene spaces are not only functional but also accessible and secure for all, especially women, children, and persons with disabilities. Key activities include conducting regular protection assessments to identify risks and vulnerabilities, strengthening community-based protection structures to empower local actors, and implementing community support projects that may include measures to enhance safe access to WASH, health and nutrition services. The project will also establish and reinforce referral mechanisms, enabling timely referrals to specialized health, nutrition and protection services for individuals at heightened risk. Through these integrated actions, the project will not only reduce the risk of waterborne disease and poor hygiene, but also actively prevent and mitigate protection threats. ltbrgt ltbrgtNRC will implement the project in partnership with two local organizations - Addition for Disaster assistant and Development (ADD) in South Kordofan and HOPE in White Nile - expanding reach and strengthening local capacity for emergency response. This localization approach supports sustainability and long-term community resilience. NRC and partners have a well-established operational presence and expertise in both WASH and protection programming across all target locations, enabling a holistic, robust response. Furthermore, NRC and local partners will closely coordinate with other health, nutrition, and protection actors on the ground to ensure interventions are harmonized and complementary. This collaborative approach maximizes impact, avoids duplication, and supports a comprehensive response that addresses both immediate WASH needs and broader health outcomes for vulnerable communities.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Provision of medical logistics support to health responders and equitable physical and functional rehabilitation services to conflict-affected populations in Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtSudan's conflict has significantly increased rehabilitation needs while severely disrupting access to health services and humanitarian supply chains. Persons with disabilities, victims of explosive ordnance, and people with conflict-related injuries face reduced access to rehabilitation care following the suspension of services at the National Authority of Prosthetics and Orthotics (NAPO) Physical Rehabilitation Centre in Khartoum, previously the country's main referral facility. At the same time, health actors in Darfur continue to face major constraints related to the storage, transportation, and management of essential medical supplies, limiting the scale, quality, and timeliness of the health response.ltbrgtTo address these challenges, Handicap International Federation (HI) will implement an integrated intervention combining physical rehabilitation services and medical logistics support.ltbrgtUnder Outcome 1, conflict-affected persons with injuries, persons with disabilities, and victims of explosive ordnance in Khartoum State will experience improved functional independence and protection outcomes through access to quality and equitable rehabilitation services. The project will restore the operational capacity of the NAPO Physical Rehabilitation Centre through rehabilitation works, accessibility improvements, provision of rehabilitation equipment and assistive products, operational support, and capacity strengthening of physiotherapists and support staff. Rehabilitation services, caregiver education, transportation support, and strengthened referral pathways with hospitals and trauma centres will improve access to care and continuity of rehabilitation services. The project will also engage Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) to support outreach, referrals, disability inclusion, and advocacy for equitable access to services.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe intervention will strengthen referral pathways between health, rehabilitation, and protection actors, improving access to care for persons with disabilities, conflict-related injuries, and EO survivors. It will restore physical rehabilitation services to improve mobility, independence, and daily functioning while reducing secondary complications and protection risks. The project will identify, assess, and refer individuals for rehabilitation, protection, and MHPSS services. Support for EO survivors will be integrated into a disability-inclusive response aligned with UNMAS, NMAC, and humanitarian coordination efforts.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtUnder Outcome 2, the provision of shared medical logistics services will improve the efficiency and responsiveness of the health response across Greater Darfur. Through Atlas Logistique, HI will provide temperature-controlled and dry storage facilities in Tawilah and Nyala, transport services for health partners, and specialized training on medical logistics. These services will help humanitarian actors maintain appropriate storage conditions, reduce supply chain disruptions, strengthen logistics capacities, and facilitate the delivery of essential health commodities to priority and hard-to-reach locations.ltbrgtThe intervention directly contributes to the priorities of the 2026 Sudan Humanitarian Fund First Standard Allocation under the Health Sector. Outcome 1 supports the restoration of a critical health facility, strengthens rehabilitation and referral pathways, and promotes disability-inclusive access to essential health services. Outcome 2 contributes to ensuring uninterrupted and pre-positioned medical supply chains and contingency stocks in priority locations, including North and South Darfur. Together, the two outcomes strengthen both the delivery of health services and the systems required to sustain them, contributing to reduced morbidity, improved access to inclusive health care, and a more coordinated and effective humanitarian health response for conflict-affected populations in Sudan.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Integrated Health and WASH support for Crisis-effected population to reduce Morbidity and Mortality in East Darfur, South Darfur and South Kordofan.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtCARE, in partnership with RDO, HOPE, and GPBC, will implement an integrated Health and WASH intervention targeting 319,531 crisis-affected people ( Girls, 57,516 Boys 54,319, Women 121,423, Men 86,273)in 13 priority localities across SD (Kas, Nyala Janoub, Nyala Shamal, As Salam, Mershing), ED (Abu Karinka, Al Firdous, Ad Du'ayn, Abu Jabra), and SK (Abassiya, Abu Jubayhah, Al Leri, Talawdi). title.narrative: Integrated Lifesaving Health, Nutrition, and WASH Services with a Protection-Centered Approach in North Darfur, Blue Nile, South Kordofan, and North Kordofan

description.narrative: ltpgtSave the Children, in partnership with SORR, AMVO, PANCARE, Saeker, and LMI, will deliver integrated life-saving interventions to vulnerable communities by providing health, nutrition, and WASH services for 166,728 people (42,704 women, 44,603 girls, 36,289 men and 43,132 boys) across North Darfur (El Fasher Tawila), South Kordofan (Kadugli, Dilling, and Abu Jubeiha), North Kordofan (Sheikan and Um Rawaba), and Blue Nile (Baw, Damazine, Ar Rusayris, Geissan, and Ar Kurmuk, including SPLM-controlled areas). The primary objective of the program is to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality among vulnerable populations in the target locations. In line with the Sudan Humanitarian Health Minimum Service Response Package (2026), SC and its partners will deliver a comprehensive package of primary healthcare and SRH services, including maternal and newborn care, child health services, management of NCDs, trauma and emergency stabilization services, and MHPSS. Through the consortium, SC will also provide medicines and medical supplies to partners. The program will further strengthen disease surveillance, early warning systems, preparedness, and rapid outbreak response capacities for cholera/AWD, hepatitis E, dengue fever, malaria, measles, and other epidemic-prone diseases. ltbrgtThe consortium will support WASH interventions in the targeted HFs, strengthening cholera preparedness, IPC measures, and the overall quality of service delivery. Community-level WASH activities will be implemented to maximize the effectiveness of cholera preparedness and response efforts, with a particular focus on hygiene promotion, community engagement, and reducing disease transmission risks. WASH interventions at the community level will be prioritized in high-risk IDP camps and displacement-affected communities in Geissan, Ar Rusayris, and Ar Rahad. title.narrative: Emergency Nutrition response in North Darfur, Sudan

title.narrative: LIFELINE-Sudan: Life-Saving Integrated Health, Nutrition and WASH Emergency Response in North Darfur, Blue Nile and Khartoum

description.narrative: ltpgtWorld Relief Sudan (WRS), Medair, Sudan Social Development Organization (SUDO), and Child Development Foundation (CDF) will deliver an integrated ltbgtHealth, WASH, Nutrition and protection-centredlt/bgt response in high severity areas of North Darfur, Blue Nile, and Khartoum. title.narrative: Provision of Integrated Life-Saving Health Services Continuity, Nutrition, WASH, and Cholera Response Services with Embedded Protection Mainstreaming in South, East Darfur and West Kordofan

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Sudan humanitarian crisis continues to drive unprecedented levels of displacement, disease outbreaks, food insecurity, and the collapse of essential services across Darfur and Kordofan. Conflict, recurrent population movements, deteriorating health infrastructure, and limited access to safe water and nutrition services have left millions of people vulnerable to preventable illness, malnutrition, and death. In response, a consortium of humanitarian organizations, Alight, AAO, WVI, Medair, CAFA, and SI, will implement an integrated, life-saving health, nutrition, WASH, and cholera response program across South East Darfur, and West Kordofan.ltbrgtThe project aims to save lives and reduce morbidity and mortality among ltbgt1,246,288lt/bgt conflict-affected, displaced, returnee, and host community members by ensuring continuity of essential health services, strengthening nutrition interventions, expanding access to safe water and sanitation, responding to cholera and other disease outbreaks, and embedding protection mainstreaming across all sectors. The intervention is designed to address immediate humanitarian needs while strengthening community resilience and service delivery systems in some of Sudan's most underserved and high-severity localities.ltbrgtThrough an integrated health response, the consortium will support 27 health facilities to deliver a comprehensive package of primary healthcare services, including outpatient consultations, communicable disease management, maternal and newborn health services, immunization, mental health and psychosocial support, trauma care, and clinical management of rape for survivors of gender-based violence. The project will strengthen disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness, referral systems, and health workers' capacity to improve access to quality, timely care.ltbrgtNutrition interventions will focus on the prevention, early detection, and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding women. The consortium will support 9 nutrition sites delivering CMAM services, including treatment of severe acute malnutrition through OTP and SC management of moderate acute malnutrition through TSFP blanket supplementary feeding in high-risk areas micronutrient supplementation and large-scale nutrition screening and referral. IYCF promotion will be strengthened through mother support groups, community outreach, and health worker training to improve feeding practices and prevent malnutrition.ltbrgtThe WASH component will improve access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services while serving as a critical pillar of cholera prevention and response. Activities will include rehabilitation and operation of water systems, emergency water supply interventions, water quality monitoring and treatment, sanitation improvements, hygiene promotion, distribution of 750 WASH and hygiene kits, operation and maintenance of 47 communal water points, establishment of 10 handwashing facilities, and infection prevention and control measures in 5 health facilities and 2 CTCs. Integrated WASH-health responses will be rapidly deployed to contain cholera, acute watery diarrhea, hepatitis E, and other waterborne disease outbreaks in priority locations.ltbrgtProtection mainstreaming will be embedded across all project activities to ensure assistance is safe, inclusive, accessible, and accountable. Special attention will be given to women, children, persons with disabilities, older persons, survivors of gender-based violence, and other vulnerable groups. CFM, AAP, safeguarding measures, PSEA standards will be implemented throughout the project cycle. By combining the technical expertise, operational reach, and community trust of international and national partners, the consortium will deliver a coordinated, multisectoral response that addresses urgent humanitarian needs, strengthens local capacities, and helps reduce preventable deaths and suffering among vulnerable populations in Darfur and West Kordofan.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Lifesaving Health and WASH Support for Vulnerable Conflict‑Affected People in North Kordofan

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project “Lifesaving Health and WASH Support for Vulnerable Conflict Affected People in North Kordofan” aims to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality among crisis affected populations in Sheikan, Um Rawaba, and Ar Rahad. Years of conflict, displacement, and service collapse have left communities without functional PHC, safe water, sanitation, or disease prevention systems. Joint IRW–JASMAR assessments confirmed severe shortages of staff, medicines, equipment, IPC supplies, and reliable water and power in health facilities. WASH assessments identified damaged handpumps, limited water access, inadequate institutional sanitation, and poor hygiene practices, disproportionately affecting IDPs, female headed households, older persons, and persons with disabilities.ltbrgtThe project will strengthen essential PHC services by supporting targeted facilities with staffing incentives, uninterrupted medical supplies, basic devices, and strengthened ANC/PNC, SRH, trauma care, and MHPSS integration. Twelve Primary Healthcare Centers (PHCs) will extend lifesaving services, will deliver outpatient consultations, maternal and child health services, immunization support, health education, and referrals for severe cases. ltbrgtDisease surveillance will be reinforced through EWARS reporting, training of frontline workers, support to rapid response teams, and provision of outbreak investigation supplies. Referral pathways will be strengthened through transportation assistance for emergency cases and vulnerable individuals. Cholera preparedness will be enhanced through support to designated treatment centres.ltbrgtWASH interventions will enhance reliable access to safe water and dignified sanitation services in targeted health facilities and surrounding communities. The project will rehabilitate water‑supply systems—including transitioning from fuel‑powered to solar‑powered pumping—restore functionality of damaged handpumps, desludge communal and institutional latrines, and reconstruct sanitation blocks using gender‑segregated and disability‑inclusive designs. Water‑quality assurance will be strengthened through routine testing, chlorination, and documentation of safety parameters. Facility‑level WASH FIT assessments and risk‑based improvement plans will reinforce IPC measures and environmental‑health standards, ensuring safer service delivery for patients, staff, and community members.ltbrgtA robust MEAL system will ensure evidence-based implementation, real-time performance tracking, and adaptive management. Routine field monitoring, service quality checks, and output verification will be conducted. Community feedback will be collected through helpdesks, hotline channels, and community meetings, enabling timely resolution of concerns and integration of community perspectives. AAP principles will guide all stages of the intervention, ensuring meaningful participation of women, youth, older persons, and persons with disabilities. Coordination will be maintained with MoH, WASH authorities, HAC, locality administrations, and cluster partners to ensure harmonized targeting, avoid duplication, and facilitate joint assessments and referrals. Access constraints will be mitigated through reliance on local partners, community volunteers, and continuous engagement with local leaders to ensure safe, negotiated access.ltbrgtOverall, the project will directly target 38,000 people through Health services and 15,000 people through WASH interventions, prioritizing IDPs, host communities, women, children, older persons, and persons with disabilities. By integrating lifesaving health and WASH services, strengthening surveillance and outbreak response, and restoring critical facility functionality, the intervention aligns with the SHF 2026 First Standard Allocation objective of reducing preventable morbidity and mortality in underserved localities of North Kordofan.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Integrated Primary Health Care, Nutrition, GBV, WASH, and Cholera Response in South and North Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtThe overall goal of this proposed intervention is to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality while enhancing the health, safety, and resilience of conflict-affected and vulnerable populations through the delivery of integrated lifesaving services. In Biliel and As Salam localities of South Darfur, the project will provide integrated Primary Health Care (PHC), nutrition, MHPSS, and gender-based violence (GBV) response services, alongside WASH, IPC, and cholera preparedness and response interventions. In As Salam locality of South Darfur and Dar As Salam locality of North Darfur, the project will strengthen access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services, infection prevention and control (IPC), cholera preparedness and response, and mainstream GBV risk mitigation and safe referral pathways to ensure protection-sensitive service delivery. The project will also support the National MHPSS Technical Working Group (TWG) Co-Cluster Coordinator role to strengthen national coordination, harmonization of MHPSS services, and improve technical guidance and quality of mental health and psychosocial support interventions across Sudan.ltbrgtThe project will provide integrated health services through two Primary Health Care Centers (PHCCs) in Umgonya and Mirer West in Biliel locality, South Darfur, serving an estimated catchment population of 43,089 people. The activities will strengthen access to essential quality PHC services, including outpatient consultations, reproductive maternal newborn and child health, routine immunization, management of communicable and non-communicable diseases, integrated mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), referral services, and outbreak preparedness and response. Nutrition services will be fully integrated into PHC service delivery and will include community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) including outpatient therapeutic programme (OTP), targeted supplementary feeding programme (TSFP), growth monitoring, maternal, infant and young child feeding (MIYCF) counselling and nutrition screening and referral services for children under five and pregnant and lactating women. ltbrgtIn South Darfur, the project will strengthen access to safe and sustainable WASH services in As Salam locality through rehabilitation and improvement of water supply systems, sanitation facilities, hygiene promotion, infection prevention and control (IPC), and health and hygiene promotion, health facility waste management and community engagement to reduce the risk of waterborne diseases and support health service continuity. In North Darfur, the intervention will strengthen cholera preparedness and response capacities in Dar As Salam locality through community-based surveillance, rapid response mechanisms, water quality monitoring and chlorination, hygiene promotion, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), and targeted WASH support to vulnerable households and communities at risk of outbreaks.ltbrgtRecognizing the heightened protection risks faced by women and girls amid ongoing conflict and displacement, the project will integrate GBV risk mitigation and response across all sectors. Activities will include community awareness raising, capacity strengthening of frontline workers, safe identification and referral mechanisms, and survivor-centered case management services through established referral pathways. Strong linkages with Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) partners, will ensure vulnerable households, women at risk, and GBV survivors have access to complementary livelihood and economic recovery opportunities that contribute to resilience and reduced negative coping mechanisms.ltbrgtThis project aims to sustain essential services, strengthen community resilience, improve preparedness and response to disease outbreaks, and ensure equitable access to life-saving assistance across some of the most underserved and high-risk areas of Darfur.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Life-saving integrated health, nutrition and community-based protection response for conflict-affected, displaced and at-risk populations in Jebel Awlia and Karari localities, Khartoum State

description.narrative: ltpgtAfter three years of conflict, Sudan continues to face one of the world’s largest humanitarian crises, marked by mass displacement, severe service disruptions, and a health system on the verge of collapse. In Khartoum State, where an estimated 75% of hospitals have been damaged or rendered inoperable, access to essential health and nutrition services remains critically limited. At the same time, recurrent disease outbreaks, including cholera, continue to exacerbate vulnerabilities and increase health risks, particularly in overcrowded and underserved areas. In response, PUI proposes an integrated Health, Nutrition, and Protection intervention aimed at reducing preventable morbidity and mortality in Karrari and Jebel Awlia localities, directly targeting a total of 18,523 and indirectly 8,100 conflict-affected, displaced, returnee, and host community members.ltbrgtltbrgtThe intervention will focus on two key pillars: ltbrgtltbgt1. Support the delivery of essential health care services at PHCC level ltbrgtlt/bgtPUI will support Al Gadisia and Al Gobba PHCC in Jebel Awlia locality, and Al Waha Shareg PHCC in Karrari locality by restoring core health services, including outpatient consultations, sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care, and Integrated Management of Childhood Illnesses (IMCI). This support will involve training of State Ministry of Health (SMoH) staff on key topics and supplying essential medicines and equipment. Light rehabilitation of the facility will also be conducted to enhance service delivery, safety, gender- and disability-inclusivity. PUI will in coordinate closely with Solidarités International for the WaSH in Health components of the PHCC light rehabilitation. Community-based awareness raising on MHPSS and the establishment of Community-Based Protection Networks (CBPNs) will be integrated alongside health and nutrition services to strengthen community resilience, promote early identification of vulnerabilities, and improve referral pathways, ultimately enhancing the overall well-being of populations within the health facilities’ catchment areas. ltbrgtltbgt2. Implement prevention and treatment services of acute malnutrition at PHCC and community level ltbrgtlt/bgtTo address acute malnutrition, PUI will support Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) for children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) without complications cases among children under five. For SAM cases with medical complication, the referrals will be supported to the nearest Stabilization Center. To prevent malnutrition, community-engagement-type of activities will also be conducted through a network of Community Health Volunteers (CHVs). These CHVs will conduct active screening in the community and track defaulters of nutrition programs and awareness-raising sessions on nutrition topics at community level. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtAligned with SHF first standard allocation strategy and recognizing the importance of the fact that a health facility cannot save lives if it lacks water, PUI is coordinating with Solidarités International to complement the WaSH in health and the Wash cholera response within PUI-supported facilities and their respective catchment area. Prioritizing the safety, dignity, and inclusion of all individuals affected by the intervention, PUI will apply a do-no-harm principle, and mainstream protection and disability inclusion across all activities. In addition to the light rehabilitations to ensure a safe and accessible environment for persons with disabilities, PUI is coordinating with Humanity Inclusion to reduce discrimination and ensure dignified access to services through the sensibilization and training of PUI staff and PHCC staff on Inclusive Humanitarian Action.lt/pgt

title.narrative: Integrated, life-saving Health, Nutrition and WASH services for conflict-affected populations in Lagawa and Alodyia localities in West Kordofan

description.narrative: ltpgtThis 12-month intervention will provide integrated, life-saving Health, Nutrition, and WASH services, for 87,038 conflict-affected people across Lagawa and Alodyia localities in West Kordofan State, Sudan. It addresses a critical funding gap threatening the continuity of life-saving services in seven health facilities, including 2 rural hospitals and 5 Primary Health Care Centres. nbsp ltbrgtThe project responds to critical humanitarian needs arising from conflict, displacement, deteriorating health systems, acute malnutrition, recurrent disease outbreaks, and inadequate WASH services. In line with the allocation strategy, it contributes to reducing preventable morbidity and mortality through an integrated, protection-centered response.nbsp ltbrgtConcern Worldwide will support seven static health facilities to deliver a comprehensive package of primary health care services, including outpatient consultations, maternal and child health, immunization, reproductive health, disease surveillance, referral services, and outbreak preparedness. The project aims to provide approximately 47,286 primary health care consultations, support 1,927 skilled deliveries, vaccinate 4,979 children and pregnant women, and facilitate referrals for women with obstetric complications and other life-threatening conditions.nbsp ltbrgtNutrition services will be integrated within the same facilities and surrounding communities to strengthen early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women. The intervention will provide life-saving nutrition services to 9,074 beneficiaries, including treatment of 1,232 children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and 2,599 individuals with Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM). Community-based screening will reach approximately 23,707 children and pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls, while 5,243 caregivers will receive Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) counselling.nbsp ltbrgtTo address disease risks and improve the quality of health and nutrition services, the project will strengthen WASH conditions in supported facilities through emergency water supply, sanitation improvements, healthcare waste management, and hygiene promotion. Approximately 25,699 people will receive hygiene promotion and WASH awareness messaging. The project will also construct or rehabilitate sanitation facilities, install handwashing facilities, improve healthcare waste management systems, and ensure safe water access through water trucking and water quality monitoring. nbsp ltbrgtCross-cutting priorities including Protection, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and Inclusion will be integrated throughout implementation. Accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms will be established in all supported facilities to ensure services remain responsive, safe, and accountable.nbsp ltbrgtThroughout the project, each Health Facility will offer integrated primary healthcare and nutrition services to community members in premises that meet IPC standards and have access to water. Additional sanitation services will be available at some facilities during the second half of the project. ltbrgtBy combining health, nutrition, and WASH interventions through a coordinated facility- and community-based approach, the project will strengthen access to essential services, improve health and nutrition outcomes, enhance outbreak preparedness, not only delivering life-saving services but also building resilience among conflict-affected populations in some of the most underserved areas of West Kordofan.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Provision of Integrated Lifesaving Health, Nutrition and WASH Services for Internally Displaced Persons and Vulnerable Host Communities in Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis one-year project will deliver integrated primary health care (PHC), nutrition services, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) interventions to provide a comprehensive, lifesaving response for the most vulnerable populations.ltbrgtThe project will deliver lifesaving PHC services to internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable host communities in Blue Nile State (BNS) and South Kordofan State (SKS) through static clinics in IDP camps, mobile outreach teams, and an integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) approach for remote and underserved areas. In Baw and Kurmuk Counties, Samaritan’s Purse will implement integrated interventions including mobile clinics, support to restore essential health services, Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH)), and sexual gender-based violence (SGBV) care, and rapid response teams providing trauma care, psychological first aid (PFA), and referrals. The project will also strengthen disease surveillance and outbreak response systems, enabling timely investigation and the establishment of emergency treatment and isolation centers during public health emergencies.lt/pgtltpgtLifesaving nutrition interventions will focus on the prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under age five (CU5s) and pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls (PBWGs), including both severe and moderate cases, through targeted, lifesaving protection and preventive nutrition services in BNS. To promote sustainability, Samaritan’s Purse will strengthen the capacity of 25 Water Management Committees (WMCs) and Hand Pump Mechanics and ensure community participation in water point planning and management.ltbrgtThe project will also support 30 HFs with infection prevention and control materials and training, distribute 600 WASH non-food items (NFIs) and 400 menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kits to vulnerable IDP households (HHs), and train 54 Health and Hygiene Promoters (HHPs) to deliver health and hygiene education to at least 27,000 people across the target communities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn total, this project aims to reach 214,625 beneficiaries across the health, nutrition, and WASH interventions.ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Emergency WASH and Cholera Response for Conflict-Affected Populations in Kass (incl. Kalo Kitting) and As Salam localities, South Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtThis integrated project delivers a coordinated, life-saving emergency WASH and Protection intervention in South Darfur’s Kass, Al Salam, and Sharg El Jabal localities, led jointly by HOPE and Acted. Fully aligned with the strategic objectives of the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), this initiative addresses a critical humanitarian crisis characterized by acute clean water shortages, widespread open defecation due to a total lack of latrines, absent vector control, and rising cases of Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD).The intervention utilizes a dual approach to support crisis-affected Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities: continuous essential service delivery to meet survival needs and a rapid response mechanism for the rainy season and cholera and Hepatits E outbreaks. Particular attention will be given to pregnant women, who face heightened risks of fulminant hepatic failure, miscarriage, stillbirth, neonatal death, and maternal mortality if infected with Hepatitis E, through targeted hygiene promotion, safe water access, and priority referral to health services. Operationally, HOPE targets high-priority locations within Kass and Al Salam localities, while Acted focuses on the rapidly expanding Kalo Kitting IDP site (hosting 10,000 displaced individuals) and surrounding catchment areas along the Kass-Sharg El Jabal administrative border, directly complementing a 10-bed Cholera Treatment Unit (CTU) operated by MSF. Context and Needs Assessment according to rapid assessments by HOPE, Water and Environmental Sanitation (WES), and OCHA, emergency WASH infrastructure is severely limited Water Scarcity: A critical shortage of safe drinking water forces households to rely on contaminated open valleys (Wadis) or single shallow wells. Sanitation Deficits: Most targeted villages completely lack latrines, resulting in widespread open defecation within water collection zones, driving high risks of fecal-oral disease transmission. Health Threats: Existing water sources are highly susceptible to seasonal contamination. Vector control is entirely absent, causing a reported surge in fly and mosquito populations. MSF reports a spike in AWD cases since April 2026.Protection Vulnerabilities: Poor infrastructure and long water collection journeys heavily impact the physical safety and wellbeing of women and children, compounding Gender-Based Violence (GBV) risks. Target Beneficiaries and Demographics the project targets the following crisis-affected populations to reduce preventable waterborne morbidity and mortality: Basic Water Services: 26,000 beneficiaries (5,606 men, 5,834 women, 7,134 boys, 7,426 girls). Sanitation and Hygiene: 100,000 beneficiaries (21,836 men, 26,644 women, 25,244 boys, 26,276 girls). Combined WASH Sector Outcomes and Outputs: Under the WASH sector, Acted and HOPE will implement coordinated interventions to improve public health and prevent outbreaks. Outcome 1: Vulnerable populations have improved, equitable, and sustainable access to safe drinking water and adequate, gender-sensitive sanitation services. Output 1.1: Rehabilitation and continuous chlorination of non-functional hand pumps, water networks, and water quality monitoring. Output 1.2: Construction of emergency, gender-segregated latrines and handwashing stations in schools, clinics, and crowded spaces. Output 1.3: Deployment of rainy-season vector control campaigns and distribution of hygiene items. Output 1.4: Formation and technical training of local water committees to ensure community ownership and maintenance. Combined Protection Sector Outcomes and Outputs complement physical infrastructure and reflect strong interlinkages, protection is mainstreamed across all activities alongside targeted interventions. Outcome 2: The safety, dignity, and rights of crisis-affected populations—particularly women, girls, and children—are protected through specialized assistance. ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Integrated Life-Saving Health and WASH Response for Conflict-Affected and Displaced Populations in Tawila Locality, North Darfur

title.narrative: Reducing morbidity and mortality among IDPs and host communities in Ad Dabah locality by providing lifesaving health services and preventing and controlling epidemics.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project aims to reduce morbidity and mortality among internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities in Ad Dabbah locality, Northern State, Sudan. Over a 12-month period, the project will deliver an integrated package of primary care, secondary referrals, and epidemic control measures. Through supporting 2nbspprimary healthcare facilities including Alafad IDPs camp clinic, the project covers the health needs of 48,000 individuals, comprising 14,688 women, 9,762 girls, 4,235 men, and 2,822 boys.ltbrgtTo ensure comprehensive, lifesaving primary and secondary healthcare access, the project invests heavily in maternal, child, and general health interventions:ltbrgtReproductive Child Health: Reproductive health efforts target 3,000 antenatal care visits, 1,440 family planning consultations, and 50 skilled-attended births, backed by essential medicine distribution and emergency obstetric referral pathways. Child survival is safeguarded through standard immunization protocols (EPI), aiming to vaccinate 1,200 children under five, including 1,061 infants targeted for the measles vaccine.ltbrgtPrimary Care Referrals: Across the supported clinics, health teams are projected to conduct 48,000 general outpatient consultations and deliver mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) to 1,910 traumatized individuals. For severe cases requiring specialized treatment, a secondary referral network will safely transfer 180 patients to higher-level facilities, such as Ad Dabbah Central Hospital, by fully subsidizing patient transportation and meal costs.ltbrgtEpidemic Control Emergency Response: The project enhances local epidemic surveillance by training 80 health staff in total: 40 personnel will be instructed on Early Warning, Alert and Response Systems (EWARS) to achieve a 90% timely reporting rate, while 60 workers will receive Rapid Response Team (RRT) training and case management protocols for cholera and dengue fever outbreaks.nbspltbrgtProtection Specialized Care: Disability inclusion activities include distributing essential mobility devices (such as walking aids and prosthetics) to 25 patients, alongside performing sight-restoring cataract surgeries for another 25 individuals. To address gender-based violence (GBV), the project will train 40 health staff and social workers on the Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) and specialized case management. These trained teams will directly provide psychosocial support to 40 GBV survivors, navigate 15 individuals through safe protection pathways, and conduct localized community awareness sessions targeting 300 people.ltbrgtIn conclusion, this project directly aligns with the allocation strategy by supporting the restoration and continuity of integrated, lifesaving, and protection-centered services in Ad Dabbah—one of Sudan's highest-severity areas (Severity 4). Specifically, the project maintains essential health services at Al Afad camp, building upon interventions previously supported under the 48-hour response framework.ltbrgtRather than delivering health interventions in isolation, the project embeds WASH and Nutrition alongside comprehensive Protection mainstreaming:ltbrgtWASH Integration: Facilities will undergo infrastructure upgrades (latrines and handwashing stations) and advance Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) practices through staff training and the provision of PPE, soap, and detergents.ltbrgtNutrition Integration: Embeds Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) center at Alafad IDPs camp PHC, Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) packages, and community outreach for MUAC screening, case identification, and active referrals.ltbrgtProtection Mainstreaming: Mainstreams GBV mitigation and targeted assistance for persons with disabilities into all project components.lt/pgt

title.narrative: Sustaining Life-Saving Health Services and Controlling Disease Outbreaks for the Affected Communities in Al Managil and Um Alqura Localities in Al Jazira State.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis integrated intervention aims to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality among IDPs, host communities, and returnees in the highest-severity conflict-affected localities of Aljazeera State. Building on CDF’s strong operational presence in Aljazeera since 2018, the project directly addresses the systemic collapse of basic infrastructure and escalating disease outbreaks (such as cholera and AWD) driven by active conflict. ltbrgtThe health component focuses on sustaining life-saving operations across 3 Health Facilities (HFs) in Al Managil and 2 HFs in Um Alqura localities, ensuring primary healthcare, maternal/newborn care, essential drug provisions, medical equipment supplies, and active trauma stabilization.ltbrgtThe WASH component systematically ensures service continuity in health facilities and targets vulnerable IDPs/communities in Al Managil amd Um Alqura localities, introducing cholera preparedness and rapid response mechanisms, rehabilitation of durable water infrastructure, hybrid solarization, mass hygiene promotion, and emergency waste management. Protection considerations, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) risk mitigation are explicitly mainstreamed through dedicated community helpdesks, targeted safety sessions, and inclusive design structures.lt/pgt

title.narrative: Provide comprehensive Life-Saving WASH Intervention for affected people by conflict and Cholera in Localities of Jabel Awlia （Khartoum stat, Kosti, and Rabak (White Nile state）

description.narrative: ltpgt2026– Emergency WASH Response for 325,000 conflict and Cholera affected people in Localities of Jabel Awlia in Khartoum state, Kosti and Rabak in White Nile state is aimed to addressing the most critical humanitarian gaps for cholera and conflict affected people in Khartoum and White Nile states localities of Jebel Awlia, Rabak and Kosti respectively. Due to the recent conflict in greater Kordofan WNS received more than 10 thousand IDPs who fled from different parts in Kordofan where conflict is escalated between SAF and RSF. 4 thousand of those IDPs were accommodated in Goz Elsalam IDPs camp in Kosti. Likewise, Khartoum state, especially Jebel Awlia locality, received a considerable number of IDPs, most of them accommodated by the host community, and there are 450 IDPs accommodated at informal camp in Wad Al Agali, Al Kalakla Al Quba and 500 IDPs in Al Hilla Al Gadeeda, Jebel Awlia. To bridge the humanitarian gaps and Cholera outbreak at the target localities, the project will fully rehabilitate and upgrade water supply system using solar energy for the three main hospitals in Alkalakla (Turkey hospital), Jebel Awlianbsp and Rabak, while constructing 6 solar water points atnbsp the 5nbsp HCFs within the IDPs camps and host communities sites (1 in Al-Shaheed Wida’Tallah PHC Centre - Wad Al Agali neighborhood, 1 in Jebal Awlia and 3 in WNS Kosti and Rabak as appropriate)nbsp and 1 IDPs canp in Al-Gadeeda Area, Jebel Awlia Khartoum state. Moreover, water collection containers will be distributed to the most vulnerable hhs (Jerrycans, Barrels, plastic Buckets and plastic jug) at the target IDPs camps in Wad Al Agali neighborhood, Al Kalakla block 2 and Al Hilla Al-Gadeeda Area, Jebel Awlia block 2 Khartoum state in addition to Goaz elsalam in Kosti locality WNS. While the project is completing the water activities water will be provided to IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Jebel Awlia and Kosti localities for two months. These four activities will be complemented by supply of 400 cartons of chlorine tablets 1.67g and 0.33g and will be provided as complement to water quality monitoring activities to ensure water quality at both hhs and water sources levels. To raise awareness of the target community about Cholera prevention measures and adopt sanitation and hygiene promotion measures as well, the project will construct 8 institutional latrines with 4 pits (4 in Khartoum and 4 in WNS), dislodge 100 institutional latrines with small maintenance (50 in Khartoum and 50 in WNS), distribute 400 HWFs in both target states (200 in Khartoum and 200 in WNS). To facilitate Hygiene Promoters tasks the project will print and distribute IEC materials to disseminate hygiene and sanitation related messages to the target beneficiaries. To improve community access to improved sanitation services, the project will conduct 20 dispose Solid and medical waste management campaigns (5 in Alkalakla, 5 in Jebel Awlia, 5 in Rabak and 5 in Kosti) to safe disposal of the medical and solid waste which will decrease number of flies and other insects accordingly cholera transmission degree will decrease as well. Moreover, to ensure to promote beneficiaries’ health benefits, the project will conduct 20 hygiene promotion sessions 10 in Khartoum and 10 in WNS including refresher training of the existing hygiene promoters at the HCFs and ministry of health, this will be done simultaneously with the 20 vector control campaigns 10 in Khartoum and 10 in WNS target the same locations. For more protection and dignity to the vulnerable people at the IDPs camps in Jebel Awlia and Kosti, the project will distribute 1000 dignity kits and 3000 mosquito nets to the most vulnerable hhs at the informal camps (500 hygiene kits and 1500 mosquito nets for each state). SOS Sahel will closely coordinate with the relevant actors to avoid resource duplication/overlap. ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Provision of Lifesaving Integrated Health and WASH Response for Vulnerable Populations in South and East Darfur States.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to deliver lifesaving, integrated Health and WASH services to 355,621 crisis‑affected people, representing 30% of the total catchment population of 1,185,403 across Kass, Mershing, Beleil, Al Radoum, Ad Du’ayn, Abu Karinka, and Al Firdous localities in South and East Darfur. Of the total target population, 67.16% will be reached through Health interventions and 32.84% through WASH interventions. These areas face severe delivery gaps following partner handovers, recurrent outbreaks of cholera, diphtheria, and measles, and chronic shortages of safe water and sanitation, leaving vulnerable populations at heightened risk of preventable illness and mortality. The health component will restore and strengthen essential primary health care through 12 PHCs and 3 mobile clinics, targeting 238,834 people. Service delivery points include Alradoum locality (Alradoum Refugee PHC, Girba PHC, Wad Haggam PHC), Kass/South Jebel Marra (Kalukitng PHC, Kara PHC, Saboon Al Fagur PHC), Beleil (Center Zero PHC, Marla PHC, Hijir Tono PHC), Ad Du’ayn (Muhajir PHC), Al Firdous (Almagareen PHC), and Abu Karinka (Alsalam PHC). Services include IMCI, ANC/PNC, emergency care, MHPSS, referral support, and strengthened outbreak detection and response. CBS and EWARS reporting will be reinforced to improve early warning and rapid response capacity, particularly in remote and rainy‑season‑isolated villages. The WASH component targets 116,787 people, improving access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services through rehabilitation and chlorination of water points, restoration of water yard functionality, hygiene kit distribution, and intensified hygiene promotion. Trained WASH volunteers will support community‑based hygiene messaging, water quality monitoring, and early identification of WASH‑related risks, particularly in high‑risk settlements such as Ad Du’ayn, Mershing, Saboon Al Fagur, Kalu Kitting, and Kass. Health and WASH interventions are fully integrated to maximize impact and reduce preventable morbidity and mortality. Outbreak preparedness and response will be jointly implemented, with PHCs and mobile clinics triggering rapid WASH actions such as chlorination, intensified hygiene promotion, and water‑quality testing when CBS/EWARS alerts indicate rising diarrheal or waterborne disease trends. Infection prevention and control will be strengthened through rehabilitation of water points at PHCs to ensure continuous safe water for handwashing, cleaning, and waste management, alongside joint IPC training for health workers and WASH volunteers. IMCI consultations will be linked with targeted hygiene promotion for caregivers of children with diarrhea, pneumonia, or skin infections. WASH volunteers will support follow‑up visits for high‑risk households identified by PHC staff. GBV risk mitigation is integrated across all Health and WASH activities, including safe facility design, improved lighting and safety around water points, PSEA training for frontline staff, and confidential referral pathways accessible through both PHC and WASH entry points. Community Health Committees, WASH volunteers, and CBS volunteers will jointly support community mobilization, hygiene promotion, surveillance, and accountability, with harmonized feedback mechanisms across PHC and WASH sites to strengthen community trust. Pre‑positioning of supplies will ensure continuity during rainy‑season isolation, and coordination with the State Ministry of Health, WES Department, locality authorities, and cluster partners will guide implementation. By restoring PHC functionality, expanding safe water access, strengthening outbreak preparedness, and embedding protection and GBV risk mitigation, the project directly contributes to Health, WASH, and GBV sector objectives and aligns with SHF 2026 Allocation Strategy priorities to reduce excess morbidity and mortality and ensure principled, inclusive, and accountable lifesaving assistance for IDPs. ltbrgtlt/pgt

title.narrative: Provision of Integrated Life-Saving Reproductive Health Supplies in Sudan's highest severity localities

description.narrative: ltpgtSudan continues to experience one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, with widespread displacement, recurrent disease outbreaks, and extensive disruption of health services severely limiting access to life-saving sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care. Conflict, insecurity, damaged infrastructure, and supply chain disruptions have resulted in persistent shortages of essential reproductive health commodities, placing women and girls at increased risk of preventable maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality.ltbrgtIn line with the Sudan Humanitarian Fund First Standard Allocation priorities, UNFPA proposes a focused intervention to ensure the uninterrupted availability of life-saving reproductive health commodities in the highest-priority localities through procurement, pre-positioning, and last-mile distribution of Inter-Agency Reproductive Health (IARH) Kits and essential reproductive health supplies.ltbrgtThe intervention will support prioritized health facilities across the prioritised SHF localities by strengthening the national emergency reproductive health supply chain. UNFPA will procure internationally standardized IARH Kits, essential reproductive health medicines, consumables, and selected reproductive health equipment required for safe delivery, emergency obstetric and newborn care, family planning, post-abortion care, and clinical management of rape.ltbrgtCommodity distribution will be coordinated with the Ministry of Health, the Sexual and Reproductive Health Technical Working Group (SRH TWG) and Health Cluster partners, and humanitarian actors to maximize coverage, avoid duplication, and maintain continuity of essential reproductive health services.ltbrgtlt/pgt
